title: Cathay Pacific and Google Partner to Research and Trial AI-Powered Contrail Avoidance
description:
-- Cathay Pacific and Google today announced a partnership to advance research on contrails and their contribution to aviation’s climate impact.
Cathay Pacific is Google’s first commercial airline partner in Asia‑Pacific to trial its AI‑powered contrail mitigation technology, and the first airline globally to test contrail avoidance on ultra‑long‑haul flights.
The companies have started trials to evaluate the operational feasibility and constraints of contrail avoidance across Cathay Pacific’s extensive global network.
Cathay Pacific and Google collaborate to advance research on contrails and contribute to aviation industry’s climate impact.
Through this partnership, Cathay Pacific and Google are supporting contrail research using real‑world operational data from flight trials.
text:
The partnership attempts to understand the operational feasibility and potential climate benefits of contrail avoidance across Cathay Pacific’s extensive global network, while contributing real world data to advance global contrail research.

-- Cathay Pacific and Google today announced a partnership to advance research on contrails and their contribution to aviation’s climate impact. Cathay Pacific is Google’s first commercial airline partner in Asia‑Pacific to trial its AI‑powered contrail mitigation technology, and the first airline globally to test contrail avoidance on ultra‑long‑haul flights. The companies have started trials to evaluate the operational feasibility and constraints of contrail avoidance across Cathay Pacific’s extensive global network. The trials will contribute valuable new data to global contrail research and advance understanding of contrail formation and avoidance in the Asia‑Pacific region, a geography that has been underrepresented in previous trials. The real‑world data gathered through the trial would allow the industry to better understand the climate benefits of contrail avoidance in actual operational environments.

Cathay Pacific and Google collaborate to advance research on contrails and contribute to aviation industry’s climate impact. (From left to right: Captain Tony Pringle, Cathay Pacific Line Operations Manager, Lawrence Fong, Cathay Director Digital and IT, Michael Yue, Managing Director and General Manager, Google Hong Kong and Kemal Armada, Product Manager, Climate & AI, Google)

The thin white lines that sometimes form behind aircraft in the sky are known as contrails, or condensation trails. They are clouds that form when aircrafts fly through certain cold and humid conditions at high altitude. While many disappear quickly, some persist and spread into broader cloud formations that can trap heat in the atmosphere. Previous research suggests these persistent contrails could account for around one‑third of aviation's total climate impact, making them an important area of study alongside carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions.

Cathay recognises aviation’s contribution to climate change and is working towards addressing the climate impacts through multiple approaches. Reducing CO₂ emissions remains a primary focus for Cathay through fleet modernisation, operational efficiency improvements and the adoption of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). At the same time, the airline recognises the importance of growing scientific understanding of non‑CO₂ climate effects, including contrails. Through this partnership, Cathay Pacific and Google are supporting contrail research using real‑world operational data from flight trials. The insights will help build further understanding of the impact and possible actions airlines can take against individual contrails, while exploring how contrail avoidance could be implemented and managed at scale across the aviation industry.

AI in the Cockpit Shows Encouraging Early Results

Google’s contrail mitigation solution combines AI‑based predictive models, satellite imagery detection tools, and extensive weather intelligence to forecast contrail‑forming zones. This actionable data allows flight dispatchers and pilots to make informed altitude adjustments navigating around these zones much like they routinely do to avoid turbulence.

Onboard, Cathay Pacific leverages its modernised fleet capabilities, combining in‑flight Wi‑Fi connectivity with its proprietary, in‑house developed Electronic Flight Folder (EFF). The EFF system equips pilots with dynamic Google contrail forecasts alongside real‑time operational parameters, enabling seamless decision‑making in the cockpit without disrupting normal operations.

An operational trial began in late 2025, with more than 100 flights targeted across Cathay Pacific's network. Over 80 flights followed contrail‑avoidance routes[1], and Google estimates that these flights achieved roughly 40% reduction in the warming impact of contrails.

The Hong Kong‑Singapore corridor was one of the routes tested, as flights in this airspace frequently encounter conditions where persistent contrails form. Early analysis indicates that minor altitude adjustments can successfully prevent contrails, with actions taken on this single route accounting for more than 50% of the trial's total climate impact.

Lawrence Fong, Director Digital and IT, Cathay said: “Aviation needs solutions to address climate change, and AI is accelerating that progress. This partnership combines Cathay’s operational expertise with Google’s world‑class AI capabilities to tackle complex sustainability challenges at scale. At Cathay, we believe innovation should deliver tangible and meaningful impact, and this collaboration sets a new benchmark for leadership in our industry.”

Michael Yue, Managing Director and General Manager, Google Hong Kong said: “At Google, we believe AI has the power to help address complex environmental challenges and our partnership with Cathay Pacific is a prime example of this in action—researching how predictive AI can be deployed in live operations to help address the climate impact of contrails with today’s aircrafts and today’s fuel. This work reflects our ongoing commitment to developing sustainable solutions that deliver lasting impact, and we’re excited to expand our trial with Cathay Pacific and continue contributing to open climate science together.”

Shaping the Future of Aviation

The initial trial provided valuable experience for integrating predictive AI data in live flight planning to support contrail avoidance at flight levels, while bringing together the operational and technical stakeholders needed to make such trials possible. While the partnership delivered encouraging results on individual flights, further trials and research are needed to assess the benefits of applying contrail avoidance measures across airlines and airspaces. The availability of such robust science evidence will enable further industry considerations and policy development by airlines, regulators, and other industry players.

Therefore, the partners are embarking on a larger second phase of flight trials to generate a broader set of real‑world operational data and further insights across Cathay Pacific’s Asia and transpacific network. Contrails.org, a nonprofit initiative dedicated to advancing the science of contrail mitigation, is also a partner in the project. The ongoing partnership aims to generate a robust operational data set to further scientific understanding of contrail avoidance and help inform future industry best practices.

Notes to Editors:

CO₂ emissions: emissions of carbon dioxide, the largest contributor to human‑caused climate change.

Contrail warming and contrail avoidance: Contrail warming refers to the warming effect caused by persistent aircraft contrails, while contrail avoidance refers to operational changes — such as adjusting a flight’s altitude or route — to reduce the likelihood of creating contrails that have a warming effect.

text:
Japan's Nippon Kaiji Kyokai, or ClassNK, said on September 8 it had issued the first certificate under its sustainable aviation fuel certification scheme, ClassNK SCS, marking full-scale operations for what it said is Asia's first International Civil Aviation Organization-approved SAF certification framework.

The certificate was issued by Nippon Kaiji Kentei QA Co., the certification body under the scheme, to lumber producer Mokkanomori Co. ClassNK said the issuance gives SAF-related businesses in Japan a domestic route to obtain certification under an ICAO-approved scheme, where they had previously been required mainly to work with overseas schemes.

ClassNK SCS was approved by ICAO in October 2024 and began operations in August 2025, making it the third certification scheme approved globally and the first in Asia. Nippon Kaiji Kentei QA, established in 1993, carried out the first certification under the ClassNK SCS framework.

Mokkanomori is a member of the Sumitomo Forestry group and works on the effective use of woody biomass resources. The company operates a lumber business and aims to promote cascading use of wood through the use of residues generated in the sawing process.

The announcement is tied to the aviation industry's compliance framework under CORSIA, ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. SAF can sharply reduce carbon dioxide emissions compared with conventional jet fuel, but for SAF to qualify under CORSIA, all SAF-related operators across the supply chain within the certification scope must be certified by bodies operating under an ICAO-approved SAF certification scheme.

Under the system, certification schemes and affiliated certification bodies verify the sustainability of businesses across the supply chain from feedstock through the blending point and issue proof of sustainability documents. ClassNK said applications for certification under ClassNK SCS are being accepted on an ongoing basis.

ClassNK, a maritime classification society with more than 120 years of history and 130 locations worldwide, plans to expand its network of certification bodies and lead the buildout of SAF certification infrastructure in Japan and the broader Asian region. The organization said that effort is intended to support international supply chains for CORSIA-eligible fuels and expand SAF supply for the decarbonization of international aviation.

title: Eni, PETRONAS Explore High-Performance Bio-Gasoline - ChemAnalyst
description:
Eni and PETRONAS have expanded their cooperation in sustainable fuels by signing a Feasibility Agreement to investigate the development of innovative, high-performance bio-gasoline.
Its existing portfolio includes commercially available HVO diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, while the company is also advancing technologies for renewable bio-gasoline.
The Malaysian energy company has experience spanning conventional fossil-based fuels and the development of sustainable, high-performance fuels designed for combustion engines.
The latest agreement builds on a broader relationship between Eni and PETRONAS in the renewable-energy sector.
For petrochemical commodities tracked by ChemAnalyst, conventional gasoline components and fossil-based naphtha could face modest long-term demand pressure if renewable bio-gasoline achieves commercial scale.
text:
Eni and PETRONAS have expanded their cooperation in sustainable fuels by signing a Feasibility Agreement to investigate the development of innovative, high-performance bio-gasoline. The agreement was signed during the 2026 Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix and will evaluate whether renewable bio-gasoline can meet the demanding technical requirements of motorsport while offering a pathway toward future commercial applications.

The feasibility study will examine the proposed bio-gasoline from several perspectives, including technical performance, market potential, sustainability credentials and compatibility with high-performance engines. The companies intend to use the established Ecofining™ technology platform developed by Eni as a starting point. Eni has used the technology since 2014 to produce HVO biofuels from renewable feedstocks.

The collaboration combines the complementary capabilities of both companies. Eni will contribute its experience in sustainable energy solutions and renewable-fuel production through its Enilive biorefineries. Its existing portfolio includes commercially available HVO diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, while the company is also advancing technologies for renewable bio-gasoline.

PETRONAS will bring its expertise in fuel formulation, engine-performance requirements and advanced product development. The Malaysian energy company has experience spanning conventional fossil-based fuels and the development of sustainable, high-performance fuels designed for combustion engines.

The latest agreement builds on a broader relationship between Eni and PETRONAS in the renewable-energy sector. The companies recently established Searah, a 50:50 independent joint venture combining selected operations in Indonesia and Malaysia. The venture includes a portfolio of 19 gas production and development assets across the two countries.

The companies are also involved in the Pengerang Biorefinery in Johor, Malaysia, through a partnership involving PETRONAS, Enilive and Euglena. The facility is expected to begin operating at significant scale by the second half of 2028, with the ability to process up to 650,000 tonnes of renewable feedstocks annually. Its planned product slate includes Sustainable Aviation Fuel, HVO diesel and bio-naphtha.

The new bio-gasoline initiative could therefore strengthen the companies' renewable-fuel portfolios beyond diesel and aviation applications. Motorsport could provide a testing environment for advanced formulations, allowing the partners to validate performance before considering wider commercial deployment.

For the transport sector, the project supports efforts to reduce the carbon intensity of internal-combustion engines without requiring an immediate transition to fully electric powertrains. If technically and commercially successful, the technology could eventually create additional demand for renewable feedstocks and expand the market for lower-carbon fuels.

Product and Chemical Commodity Price Impact

The development is bullish for biofuels and renewable-feedstock demand over the medium to long term, although the immediate price impact should remain limited because the project is still at the feasibility stage. Successful commercialization could increase demand for vegetable oils, waste oils, renewable hydrocarbons and bio-naphtha, potentially supporting their prices. HVO and SAF markets could also gain from broader investment in renewable-fuel capacity. For petrochemical commodities tracked by ChemAnalyst, conventional gasoline components and fossil-based naphtha could face modest long-term demand pressure if renewable bio-gasoline achieves commercial scale. However, near-term chemical prices are unlikely to move significantly based solely on this agreement.

text:
PAL-V ©

Dutch company PAL-V has obtained its European Production Organisation Approval (POA). With this milestone, PAL-V now holds both the automotive and aviation production approvals required to manufacture its products on an industrial scale. This approval authorises PAL-V to manufacture aviation products under EASA regulations and marks a significant step toward bringing certified FlyDrive mobility solutions to market.

PAL-V is the first company in the FlyDrive segment of Advanced Air Mobility to receive this approval, placing the company in a unique position worldwide, ahead of both American and Chinese initiatives within the Advanced Air Mobility sector.

European Aviation Authority Gives Green Light to Complete Certification

PAL-V has ensured compliance with existing regulations across all areas of its development programme. With the achievement of its POA, PAL-V has successfully completed several critical certification milestones, including receiving a “No Technical Objection” from EASA in 2025. These certification achievements confirm PAL-V's leading position in the emerging FlyDrive market and demonstrate the maturity of the company, its technology and its products.

Professionals' Mobility Challenges Are a Growing Global Problem

Whether it involves saving lives, deploying specialists to remote locations or transporting critical goods, traditional mobility solutions force operators to choose between, or combine, road and air transport. This results in delays, additional complexity and operational inefficiencies. FlyDrive products provide a unique solution to this challenge. They are the only vehicles capable of transporting professionals at flight speed while offering the flexibility of a car immediately after landing. As such, a FlyDrive vehicle represents a valuable capability for organisations where speed, accessibility and operational effectiveness are critical.

Leadership Through Certification and Execution

The Production Organisation Approval confirms that PAL-V's production system meets the stringent requirements for airworthy manufacturing. This milestone validates nearly two decades of development of certification experience and regulatory expertise that have established the company as the clear leader in the emerging FlyDrive market.

"Obtaining the POA is a major milestone for PAL-V," said Robert Dingemanse, Founder and CEO of PAL-V. "It confirms that we have not only developed a groundbreaking platform for FlyDrive products but have also built a world-class organisation capable of developing, certifying and manufacturing airworthy products."

A Dutch Ecosystem with European Significance

The development of PAL-V extends far beyond a single product. Around the company, a growing ecosystem has emerged consisting of Dutch and European partners, suppliers, knowledge institutions and certification specialists. The expertise developed in aviation certification, manufacturing, engineering and regulation represents a valuable strategic asset for both the Netherlands and Europe within the rapidly expanding Advanced Air Mobility industry.

PAL-V also integrate developments in autonomous flight, advanced materials and components, and zero-emission propulsion systems which are driving a wave of innovation entering the aviation market through this emerging sector. Through its activities, PAL-V contributes to strengthening European technological autonomy while safeguarding high-value knowledge, employment and industrial capabilities, thereby supporting the future economic competitiveness of both the Netherlands and Europe.

Creating a New Mobility Category

With its Production Organisation Approval secured and a reservation portfolio sufficient to fill the first three years of production, PAL-V has taken a major step towards creating an entirely new mobility category that enables professionals to overcome operational challenges more quickly, efficiently and effectively.

As a result, the Netherlands once again has an aircraft manufacturer with international potential, and a technology company whose capabilities and ecosystem are of strategic importance to Europe.

text:
CPM|Crown has grown over the last 150 years to become a leader in edible oilseed processing and extraction. We sit down with the company’s senior leadership team, who shed light on its revolutionary Monarc Clean Oilseed Processing™ extraction technology.

ENACTING CHANGE IN EDIBLE OILS

As a trusted global leader in oilseed extraction, CPM|Crown provides advanced technologies, processing equipment, services, and solutions for industries including food, feed, aqua, energy, industrial, and specialty products.

More specifically, these markets focus on oilseed processing, including the extraction of soybeans, canola, sunflower, and other oilseeds; green energy and renewable fuels, such as biodiesel and renewable diesel; food, feed, and aquaculture, comprising food-grade processing, specialty proteins, animal feed, and aqua feed; and chemical and pharmaceutical applications, which utilize specialized solid-liquid separation, oleochemical production, and specialty processing across many diverse products.

The company offers a comprehensive portfolio of oilseed refining and processing solutions. Prior to refining, oil must be extracted from the oilseeds, which involves seed preparation, solvent extraction, and desolventization processes.

Seed preparation includes cleaning, dehulling, conditioning, cracking, and flaking, each critical to enabling effective extraction. Proper seed preparation is critical to enable effective extraction.

Next, the extraction process uses a counter-current flow where prepared flakes and liquid solvent (hexane) wash in opposite directions inside an efficient and reliable Crown extractor. The liquid stream yields a rich mixture of oil and solvent called miscella, alongside the solvent-wet solid meal.

The meal is desolventized and toasted for use as a feed ingredient, while the miscella is pumped to the distillation process to separate the solvent from the crude oil. The solvent is subsequently reused in the process. Meanwhile, the oil undergoes a stripping process to remove any residual solvent – making it available as crude oil feedstock for further refining.

In the oil refining process, the first step involves degumming the oil to remove phospholipids and other components. From there, neutralizing steps remove free fatty acids and bleaching removes color bodies and residual impurities, creating a lighter appearance.

Deodorizing strips volatile compounds to secure a stable, palatable flavor profile, while also improving the color. Finally, crude filtration and winterizing involve the removal of solid impurities and wax fractions, respectively.

“This detailed refining process ensures the customer can provide high-quality products on a consistent basis,” opens Bill Morphew, VP Sales – Liquids Segment.

CPM’s vast global structure is supported by over 1,700 employees from its international headquarters and Global Innovation Center in Blaine, Minnesota, as well as worldwide locations such as the UK, Netherlands, Argentina, Brazil, and China.

FEEDING A BETTER WORLD

Increasing biofuel demand, feedstock volatility, tighter quality standards, and evolving sustainability expectations are continuing to shape the edible oil refining sector in North America.

As a result, food applications remain essential, while other sectors such as renewable diesel, biodiesel, and sustainable aviation fuel compete for soybean oil, canola oil, used cooking oil, animal fats, and other feedstocks.

This restricted supply environment is pushing refiners to improve yield, flexibility, uptime, and feedstock optionality, and adapt to changing crush margins, where oil has gained strategic importance, and the food produce markets move more independently.

Within this landscape, CPM|Crown plays a key role, equipped with a portfolio spanning oilseed processing, edible oil refining, specialty oils and fats, and biofuel pretreatment.

Crown is a brand division of the CPM organization whose systems support core refining steps such as degumming, neutralizing, bleaching, deodorizing, winterizing, dewaxing, enzymatic degumming, hydrogenation, fractionation, and fat modification.

By helping refiners process variable crude oils, remove key impurities, protect yield, and maintain product stability, CPM|Crown supports the industry’s move toward more flexible, efficient, and sustainable refining capacity.

“CPM|Crown’s full suite of solutions positions the company as a strategic partner in a market where food, fuel, and sustainability priorities increasingly overlap,” Morphew outlines.

SUSTAINABLE AND ECONOMICAL

In October last year, CPM|Crown launched Monarc Clean Oilseed Processing™ (Monarc™) – a leading alcohol-based solvent extraction technology.

Monarc™ provides customers with a competitive advantage because it solves the central trade-off that has limited the clean oilseed processing sector for decades.

“Processors have wanted safer, more sustainable, clean-label alternatives to petroleum-derived hexane, but alcohol-based systems historically struggled to match hexane’s economics at commercial scale.

“Monarc™ changes that by combining a patented ethanol-based extraction process with the scale, economic viability, and familiar plant configuration customers expect from modern Crown crush and protein plant offerings,” highlights Marc Ulery, Global Product Director – Monarc™.

Historically, hexane became the industry standard because of its efficient, high-volume, and affordable oil extraction qualities. However, Monarc™’s use of ethanol maintains these attributes while also ensuring cleaner production, with a process that is on par from both a capital investment and an operational cost perspective.

This allows Monarc™ to be positioned as much more than a niche sustainability upgrade, but a commercially viable platform for mainstream oilseed processors.

The technology’s aforementioned characteristics also make adoption easier for processors, investors, and engineering teams because it does not ask them to choose between sustainability and economics.

Moreover, the design and operation of Monarc™ oilseed processing facilities are very similar to Crown’s existing crush or protein plant offerings. This makes the solution more familiar to customers evaluating retrofits, brownfield improvements, or greenfield construction and presents it as an evolution of established extraction infrastructure rather than a risky departure to an unfamiliar processing platform.

“Crown provides us with the process know-how needed to make ethanol extraction economically viable while leveraging established and well-known technologies. This combination reduces perceived technology risk and improves our ability to win strategic projects,” Ulery points out.

CLEAN-LABEL MOVEMENT

The clean-label movement continues to permeate the food and beverage industry, with consumer awareness around food production processes growing, and the edible oil sector playing a key part in this increased focus. Fortunately, Monarc™ closely aligns with the consumer-driven shift.

“As expectations on food manufacturers continue to rise, Monarc™ creates a market-facing advantage by supporting the production of high-value clean-label ingredients and products, including the potential for organic labeling, which are permitted by supply chain and regulatory compliance,” Ulery informs us.

The technology’s use of ethanol, which is already associated with food and beverage applications, gives processors a more consumer-aligned processing story compared to petroleum-derived hexane.

This also supports the goals of brand owners and ingredient suppliers as they seek to communicate simpler processing, cleaner ingredients, and more responsible production.

Such advantages extend across a broad range of markets, including oils, meals, white flakes, protein concentrates, animal nutrition products, and biofuel-related value chains, all of which can benefit from a hexane-free processing narrative.

“The potential for clean manufacturing strengthens CPM|Crown’s value proposition beyond equipment sales by giving customers a scalable route into premium, differentiated markets and helping them advance broader growth strategies tied to cleaner, more responsible manufacturing,” he expands.

CIRCULAR CARBON MODEL

As a clean oilseed processing technology, Monarc™ also offers a meaningful environmental step forward by enabling ethanol extraction as an alternative to petroleum-derived hexane.

Because ethanol can be produced from plant-derived renewable sources, the technology enables processors to better align extraction operations with corporate sustainability goals, renewable energy strategies, and broader industry decarbonization commitments, while also being more scalable, efficient, and economical.

Renewable ethanol additionally supports a departure from fossil-based extraction solvents in favor of a more circular carbon model.

“Alcohol-based extraction can draw on agricultural or bio-based ethanol supply, reducing exposure to fossil-carbon inputs while allowing producers to maintain scale.

“Rather than introducing additional petroleum-derived solvent demand into the production chain, alcohol extraction draws on an agricultural-based ethanol supply, helping processors reduce exposure to fossil-carbon inputs,” explains Ulery.

This ultimately supports decarbonization while allowing producers to maintain the processing scale their businesses require.

Monarc™’s alcohol-based approach also creates practical advantages for permitting and environmental review.

In the US, hexane appears on the Environmental Protection Agency’s List of Hazardous Air Pollutants. Ethanol is not identified as such, making it better-positioned for facilities facing tighter air emissions targets, regulatory uncertainty, or heightened community scrutiny.

Furthermore, for producers located in populous areas or markets where permitting timelines and public acceptance can influence project viability, using ethanol can support a smoother path through environmental approvals and reduce the perceived risk associated with new extraction capacity.

SAFETY ADVANTAGES

Monarc™ also offers myriad workplace safety advantages, helping customers transition from petroleum-based hexane exposure risks to an alcohol-based process, which has more favorable safety and handling properties.

“By eliminating toxic hexane exposure concerns, the technology can improve plant safety profiles and essentially remove risks of processing with hydrocarbons, which is traditionally used to strip or clean any residual hexane from the oil,” Ulery tells us.

On top of this, ethanol is non-toxic and not classified as a carcinogen, thus reducing worker health risks during operations, maintenance, material handling, and storage.

It also provides an added fire safety advantage because the chemical’s autoignition temperature of 363 degrees Celsius (°C) is significantly higher than hexane’s at 223°C, creating a wider margin against unintended ignition.

Furthermore, since water is miscible in ethanol, sprinkler or deluge systems can both cool and dilute it, while water applied to hexane can only provide cooling and cannot dilute the solvent.

These advantages support customer goals around worker safety, operational risk reduction, and responsible manufacturing.

As such, for processors facing growing expectations around safety, the operating profile of Monarc™ can become a meaningful project driver.

“By enabling safer, more confident day-to-day operations, the technology creates an opportunity for increased employee engagement, stronger safety culture, and improved conditions for successful plant performance,” Ulery notes.

CONNECTING INNOVATION AND EXECUTION

CPM|Crown’s Global Innovation Center provides a low-risk path to develop, validate, scale, and commercialize new products and processes.

Located at its Blaine headquarters in Minnesota, the 15,000-square-foot pilot plant, analytical lab, and training facility replicate production environments while providing expert support, confidential testing space, and full-scale processing insight.

The company’s world-class value comes from combining production capability with deep technical expertise. With systems for preparation, extraction, and liquids refining, customers can progress from feasibility work to continuous pilot-plant testing with data representative of commercial operations.

The Global Innovation Center operates 24 hours a day, five days a week, enabling scale-up testing under production conditions.

It offers a complete innovation ecosystem with an analytical lab, engineering, fabrication, piloting, and R&D teams translating results into process designs, equipment selections, and return on investment (ROI) analysis for efficient implementation.

Through the center, CPM|Crown combines forward-thinking, proprietary technology, engineering knowledge, aftermarket experience, and full-scale support to help customers anticipate megatrends, improve continuously, and bring products to market with confidence.

The facility also strengthens workforce readiness through classroom and hands-on training in controlled environments that mirror plant realities whilst reducing risk and disruption.

“The Global Innovation Center connects innovation with execution. It gives producers a state-of-the-art production plant for innovation, real-world testing before implementation, engineering, ROI analysis, confidential product sampling, and workforce training,” surmises Alex Danelich, CCO.

ADDITIONAL PRIORITIES

With Monarc™ moving from the development stages into commercial execution, the first commercial plant contract was awarded to Elian in Barcelona, Spain in August last year.

CPM is supplying equipment for Elian’s commercial-scale facility expansion to produce soy protein concentrate at the Port of Barcelona, supporting clean-label, plant-based protein production capacity using Monarc™’s alcohol-based extraction system.

Elsewhere, the company is continuing to advance equipment innovations that improve reliability and efficiency in oilseed processing plants.

For example, Crown’s Flexible Control Tray™ Oil Stripper maximizes active tray areas while reducing the risk of fouling and plugging that can lead to costly shutdowns.

Initially focused on stripping hexane from crude oil, the technology is expanding into additional applications where improved stripping performance, uptime, and energy efficiency are priorities.

“Compared with conventional disc-and-donut style systems, it can deliver a 35 percent or greater reduction in energy requirements while maintaining or improving residual hexane performance, and its adjustable orifice layout provides flexibility across different plant conditions and operational rates,” details Danelich.

With customers looking to purify and pretreat renewable oil feedstocks for sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel production, CPM|Crown’s projects demonstrate how it is positioning its technologies to support both conventional oilseed processors and emerging renewable fuel markets.

EXCITING NEW ERA

Looking ahead, Rosebank Industries’ recent acquisition of CPM marks an important new chapter for the company, bringing a renewed focus on long-term growth, commercial discipline, and the customer experience across the full equipment lifecycle.

“As CPM becomes part of Rosebank Industries, the transition is an opportunity to strengthen its core commitments. The coming year will be defined by a clearer emphasis on helping customers maximize the value of their equipment well beyond the original sale with practical support that keeps their operations running confidently, reliably, and efficiently,” Kris Knudson, President, sets out.

The acquisition will be most visible in the company’s aftermarket support – comprising service, parts, components, technical expertise, rapid downtime response, and refurbishment – which will lead to clearer processes, stronger parts planning, and reduced lead times.

Utilizing Rosebank Industries’ resources, CPM will strengthen its delivery across key markets by combining local expertise with its broader engineering, technology, and technical network to help customers extend equipment life, improve uptime, and reduce unplanned downtime.

Customers will also benefit from a stronger CPM that has a greater ability to support equipment performance over time. The organization’s future priorities are aimed at extending equipment life, improving uptime, and delivering more predictable support through better processes and planning.

“With Rosebank Industries’ backing, CPM is positioned to combine commercial focus, local service, global resources, and technical expertise in a way that reinforces its commitment to long-term customer value,” Danelich concludes.

text:
Out at RNZAF Base Ohakea, an NH90 Tactical Troop Helicopter designated TNZA002 has quietly written aviation history. On Wednesday, 26 August 2026, the aircraft clocked 3,000 flight hours, the first NH90 anywhere on the globe to pass the 3,000 flight hour mark.

Leading the global NH90 fleet

Out of roughly 530 NH90 aircraft in active service across multiple configurations worldwide, New Zealand's No. 3 Squadron leads the entire international fleet. Remarkably, the squadron achieves this global benchmark from a base of just eight operational aircraft.

The world record is not a matter of product age, as older NH90 airframes continue to fly across Europe, but rather a reflection of pure operational intensity. Fifteen years after the first two NH90s arrived in New Zealand in December 2011 to replace the Air Force's ageing Iroquois fleet, the Kiwis fly each aircraft harder and more frequently than any other operator.

“It's a significant achievement for what is a small fleet and small team,” NH90 Flight Commander Squadron Leader Lachie Johnston said.“We need to always have these aircraft available to fly and it's a testament to the maintainers, who put in the long days in often trying conditions to get the helicopters flying, as well as the supply chain, and the fleet planners. “They are the secret sauce to our success.”

Built for the frontlines: Disaster relief to alpine mission

The New Zealand NH90 fleet is unique, as it supports a broad range of both civil and military missions. From tactical troop transport, search and rescue, casualty evacuation, and support for police and government agencies, to complex alpine tasks, maritime deployments off HMNZS Canterbury, and humanitarian disaster relief across the Pacific, the fleet is in constant demand.

This extraordinary rate of effort has been repeatedly demonstrated during some of the nation's most severe natural disasters.

When the November 2016 Kaikōura earthquake severed every road into the region, RNZAF NH90s established an emergency air bridge by midday. Patrick Power, Airbus Team Lead for the NH90 programme and the only person in New Zealand to have worked continuously on the platform since its introduction in 2011 across both uniformed RNZAF and civil roles, was right in the middle of the response.

He recalls arriving in Christchurch that evening with three NH90s to deliver critical aid and evacuate stranded civilians. "Trucks would arrive with aid and we would load it onto the helicopter, they would depart for Kaikōura, and return with a full load of people," Power recalls. "We would load it again, repeating that cycle many times a day." Maintainers also had to keep up with the intense pace on the ground.

"I always remember we had to clean the windscreen every time they came back because there were so many other helicopters in the sky doing rescue work that any small black mark looked like another aircraft," Power says. "The rate of effort was intense as we had to perform all the maintenance and get them ready for the next day, but it was very rewarding because you knew you were making a difference."

A similar story unfolded during Cyclone Gabrielle in February 2023. When the Commanding Officer of No. 3 Squadron walked into the maintenance office asking how many aircraft could be readied, a surveying NH90 had just radioed back requesting maximum assistance as floodwaters rose rapidly around trapped residents.

Power was serving as Hangar Manager at the time, in charge of day-to-day maintenance when the maintenance team made seven of the fleet's eight helicopters available that day. With the eighth airframe mid-servicing, a full 100 percent of available aircraft deployed into harm's way.

Over the course of the disaster response, No. 3 Squadron crews evacuated 384 people and 23 pets, many winched directly from the roofs of submerged homes, while transporting 25,600 kilograms of external and 66,810 kilograms of internal cargo. Coupled with emergency deployments during the 2019 Whakaari White Island eruption and the 2020 Australian bushfires, the high demand placed on the airframes is clear.

Airbus and RNZAF maintenance

Sustaining such high operational outputs requires an exceptional maintenance foundation. Since 2015, Airbus Helicopters has provided an embedded workforce that sits directly inside the RNZAF's own maintenance organisation at Ohakea.

Working as a single unit alongside Air Force mechanics like Aviator Warren Bignoux, who carries out system checks and overhauls as part of his path toward becoming a licensed engineer, this joint Deeper Maintenance team performs the major 600 flight hour servicings that take approximately three months per airframe.

Power, who trained on the type in Marignane in early 2011 and helped establish the initial deeper maintenance line in 2015 alongside Airbus specialists from Brisbane before transferring to Airbus himself in 2017, has seen the embedded workforce grow from four to ten personnel. This stable, long-tenured team provides continuity of knowledge that directly feeds training, repair development, procedure updates, and technical risk assessments.

The tangible result of this integrated approach is remarkable availability. RNZAF NH90 fleet serviceability consistently runs at around 75 percent, far surpassing the global operator average.

Thanks to this outstanding standard of technical support, the Ohakea team locally performed a major fleet-wide software upgrade (Software Release 2) in record time. And as a result, New Zealand became the first country in the world to complete the upgrade across its entire fleet.

For Power, maintaining the platform remains a deeply engaging mission. He shares that honestly, the thing he likes about the NH90 is the challenge of continuous improvement to keep the TNZA fleet as the exemplary model for NH90 operations. Even though he has been working on this type for 15 years, there is still something new almost every day and he is still learning.

That passion is shared by Airbus avionics technician Alexandra "Allie" Thompson, who has spent two and a half years on the Airbus embedded team focusing on 600-plus hour checks for the NH90.

Thompson explains that her role involves regular maintenance and repairs. "Because they're an older aircraft and not brand new, there's always going to be something fun to fix," she says.

She describes it as a very unique job from her perspective, pointing out that not often do you get to work on the mighty beast of an NH90 as a civilian person.

Thompson also highlights the broader horizon that comes with the role, sharing that she really enjoys working for Airbus because being an international company, there are obviously international opportunities available and a wider network to be a part of, which opens up many doors for future possibilities.

Through extreme weather, tactical missions, and long-range Pacific flights, New Zealand's small fleet continues to demonstrate that high standards and close collaboration yield world-leading results.

Backed by an integrated maintenance team in Ohakea, airframe TNZA002's flight hour record stands as proof that a dedicated team and an extraordinary rate of effort can set the benchmark for the rest of the world to follow.

text:
Key Takeaways:

The Senate Agriculture Committee's farm bill, the Agricultural Act of 2026, modernizes essential farm programs, authorizes year-round sales of E15 to strengthen markets for American agriculture, and includes measures to help reduce input cost volatility. As farmers and ranchers navigate one of the most challenging farm economies in a generation, this legislation provides much-needed certainty and support. The Senate Agriculture Committee should advance the bill in a bipartisan manner.

The farm bill is one of the most significant pieces of legislation affecting food and agriculture. While Congress reauthorizes the legislation every five years, the 2018 farm bill has been extended three times, and the current extension will expire on Sept. 30, 2026.

Through reconciliation in H.R. 1, the farm safety net and some conservation and research programs typically addressed in a farm bill received significant investment. Farmers and ranchers are thankful for the investments in risk management programs that will be felt on the farm this fall. However, hundreds of programs still must be updated in a full, 12-title farm bill. As farmers navigate one of the most challenging farm economies in a generation, they need the certainty that comes with a modern, comprehensive farm bill.

The Road to a New Farm Bill

In the 118th Congress, the House Agriculture Committee advanced the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024 out of committee, but it was not taken up on the House floor. The Senate Agriculture Committee also released legislative text but did not hold a markup to consider it. In this current 119th Congress, Chairman G.T. Thompson released the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which passed the House floor on a bipartisan vote of 224-200, marking the first time a farm bill passed the House floor since 2018.

Sen. John Boozman (R-Ark.), chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee, released updated text on July 31 for his farm bill.

Aug. 6 Senate Ag Committee Farm Bill Markup

On Aug. 6, the Senate Ag Committee held a markup of the Agricultural Act of 2026, but the bill failed to advance. Various amendments were debated, voted on, and agreed to throughout the markup. A bipartisan en bloc package including 34 amendments was agreed to favorably via voice vote. These amendments included several Farm Bureau priorities of, including transferring the Food for Peace Program from the Department of State to USDA. Several standalone amendment votes were taken, including a favorable 17-6 vote for Leader Thune’s amendment to require USDA and USTR to determine a path forward to re-establish mandatory country of origin labeling requirements for beef in a manner compliant with the U.S.’s obligations under the World Trade Organization. Despite the bipartisan amendment process, the bill failed to advance out of committee during this markup due to partisan gridlock over the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) state cost share. Chairman Boozman recessed the committee allowing him to bring the members back to consider the legislation when the Senate is back in session in September.

The Time is Now for a 5-Year Farm Bill

Farm Bureau believes Chairman Boozman’s farm bill includes important support for farm families across the country, and the Senate Agriculture Committee should quickly advance this bill out of markup in a bipartisan manner. Farm Bureau is also calling on Congress to address priorities that are not currently included in the draft: protecting interstate commerce from a patchwork of state laws and providing economic assistance to farmers facing historic production costs and financial losses.

Agriculture is important to the nation's economy, energy security, environment, and national security, and must be treated as a strategic national resource in policy at every level. A comprehensive five-year bill is essential to providing certainty for farmers and ranchers, strengthening rural communities, and protecting the nation's food and agricultural security.

Below is an overview of key provisions within each title of the current Senate Agriculture Committee farm bill (note: this does not include amendments debated during the Aug. 6 markup). AFBF grassroots policy is also included below for reference.

Title I: Commodities

Strengthens assistance for producers:

Upfront Tree Assistance Program payments for orchardists/nursery growers to plant alternative varieties, planting densities, and locations.

A sales-based framework for timely assistance to specialty crop producers during market disruptions or economic crises.

State block grants for uncovered livestock, poultry, crop, and tree disaster losses.

Supports a robust farm safety net:

Continues marketing assistance and sugar loans during funding lapses.

Reauthorization of key dairy programs through 2031, including the Dairy Forward Pricing Program, Dairy Indemnity Payment Program, and Dairy Promotion and Research Board.

Codifies dairy processing cost reporting.

Improves producer flexibility and risk management for elevated input costs:

Expands storage facility loans for propane, fertilizer, and related equipment.

USDA evaluation of new safety net options for dry bean producers.

Title II: Conservation

Strengthens conservation programs:

Reauthorizes the Conservation Reserve Program with reformed rental rates targeting marginal land.

Drought-related updates across conservation programs.

Enhances land conservation efforts:

Creates new programs supporting forest land and state/local conservation initiatives.

Improves easement administration to protect working farms, grasslands, and wetlands.

Improves program delivery for farmers:

Streamlines Technical Service Provider certification for broader access to conservation planning.

Title III: Trade

Helps expand markets for American farmers:

Builds on H.R. 1 export promotion investments by directing the new funding to the Market Access program and the Foreign Market Development program.

Supports international food assistance efforts:

Bolsters U.S. agricultural products through reauthorization and support of international food assistance efforts such as the McGovern-Dole Food for Education Program, Food for Progress, and the Bill Emerson Humanitarian Trust.

Addresses trade barriers

Prioritizes the protection of common food names in foreign markets and strengthens USDA’s support for specialty crop exports.

Title IV: Nutrition

Expands access to U.S. farm products:

Reinforces buy American requirements, allows all forms of fruits and vegetables to be purchased by low-income families, enhances dairy incentives for SNAP purchases, and bolsters the commodity distribution program.

Supports science-based dietary guideline review.

Strengthens local and regional food systems:

Creates a USDA-state cooperative agreement program to boost local food purchasing.

Supports SNAP program integrity:

1-year delay in implementation of the SNAP state benefit cost-share passed in H.R. 1.

Makes SNAP online purchasing permanent and supports enhanced cybersecurity efforts to prevent fraud.

Supports staffing for SNAP administration.

Title V: Credit

Expands access to agricultural credit:

Increases Farm Service Agency direct and guaranteed loan limits.

Updates the guaranteed ownership loan inflation benchmark to reflect current land values.

Improves financing for farmers, exporters, and commercial fishing operations.

Strengthens support for farmers:

Makes it easier for beginning and distressed farmers to access financing.

Expands the USDA Conservation Loan Program for precision agriculture equipment.

Modernizes rural lending:

Accelerates USDA loan delivery.

title: Major Milestone for Australian-Made SAF, Backed by Qantas and Airbus - autoevolution
description:
Australia is one of the countries that wants, and has the potential to become one of the global leaders in SAF production – not relying on external SAF supply, but gradually building its own.
Project Ulysses is the code name for a brand-new commercial-scale refinery in Townsville, Queensland, that will produce ATJ SAF and RD (Renewable Diesel).
ATJ refers to a specific SAF production pathway, alcohol-to-jet.
LanzaJet is providing its know-how in the ATJ SAF conversion technology, and Jet Zero Australia is building the actual refinery.
Project Ulysses is already one of the largest and most advanced ATJ SAF projects in the world.
text:
Project Ulysses, one of the most important Australian initiatives for commercial-scale SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) production, has reached a major financial milestone that will allow it to advance toward the actual refinery construction, with support from global investors.

As Ed Mason, chief executive officer at Jet Zero Australia, put it, the big question about SAF from a geostrategic perspective simply comes down to who will simply buy low-carbon fuels and who will invest in actually building and expanding a low-carbon fuel industry. Australia is one of the countries that wants, and has the potential to become one of the global leaders in SAF production – not relying on external SAF supply, but gradually building its own.

Jet Zero Australia is one of the startups committed to making that happen. In true startup fashion, it started in 2021 with just a handful of employees, and is now getting serious funding from top-level global and national investors, including Airbus and Qantas.

The latest $30 million funding round, which will help propel Project Ulysses toward the final refinery construction phase, has welcomed another strategic global investor, the South Korean POSCO International. The grand plan behind POSCO’s investment is the gradual extension of a co-developed SAF supply chain that will serve both Australia and South Korea.

Project Ulysses is the code name for a brand-new commercial-scale refinery in Townsville, Queensland, that will produce ATJ SAF and RD (Renewable Diesel). ATJ refers to a specific SAF production pathway, alcohol-to-jet. LanzaJet, another Australian partner in Project Ulysses, has developed the officially certified ATJ process.

ATJ is considered an even more sustainable alternative to the established SAF HEFA (hydro-processed esters and fatty acids) pathway. HEFA uses resources like cooking oil, tallow, and oil-seed crops, while ATJ uses ethanol feedstock that is more widely available.

Project Ulysses promises big things, like producing one-sixth of the domestic airline industry’s entire 2030 SAF commitment, and reducing aircraft emissions by more than 70% compared to conventional jet fuel. For the local community, it’s also expected to support more than 18,000 jobs by 2040, from feedstock production to refining and logistics.

Qantas and Airbus first announced their “Sustainable Aviation Fuel Partnership” in 2022. Their initial investment, along with additional funding from the Queensland government, was used for the feasibility study of the future refinery. LanzaJet is providing its know-how in the ATJ SAF conversion technology, and Jet Zero Australia is building the actual refinery.

Project Ulysses is already one of the largest and most advanced ATJ SAF projects in the world. In addition to it, Jet Zero is developing several other low-carbon fuel projects, including Project Mandala (a HEFA SAF refinery in Gladstone), and Silvo Plus, an agricultural business model focused on supplying feedstock for future SAF industries.

text:
By Staff Writer

Eni and Petronas have signed a Feasibility Agreement to evaluate the development of innovative high-performance bio-gasoline from renewable feedstocks, strengthening their collaboration on sustainable fuels and supporting the decarbonisation of transport.

Signed during the 2026 Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix, the agreement will assess the technical, market and sustainability aspects of new bio-gasoline products, as well as their performance in motorsport applications.

The study will explore their potential use in racing before supporting the development of commercial products for wider markets.

The technology under evaluation builds on Eni’s Ecofining process, which has been used since 2014 to produce hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biofuels from renewable raw materials.

Eni will contribute its experience in sustainable energy solutions and biofuel production through its Enilive biorefineries, which produce commercially available HVO diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), alongside its work on next-generation bio-gasoline.

PETRONAS will provide expertise in fuel technologies, including the development of high-performance sustainable fuels for combustion engines, as well as experience in sustainable energy solutions and advanced product development.

The agreement builds on several existing areas of cooperation between the two companies.

Eni and Petronas recently established Searah, a 50:50 joint venture combining operations in Indonesia and Malaysia, including 19 gas production and development assets.

The companies are also partners with Euglena through Pengerang Biorefinery Sdn. Bhd., which is developing a biorefinery in Pengerang, Johor, Malaysia.

The facility is expected to process up to 650,000 tonnes of renewable feedstocks annually by the second half of 2028, producing SAF, HVO diesel and bio-naphtha.

Enilive currently distributes HVO diesel at more than 1,700 service stations across Europe, highlighting Eni’s established position in renewable fuel production.

title: Singapore's Changi Airport locks in 'green tax' on all flights - Executive Traveller
description:
Singapore will become the first country in the world – but almost certainly not the last – to impose a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) levy onto all flights departing the island nation.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore says the fee will apply to all flights booked from 1 October 2026, for flights departing from 1 January 2027.

text:
Singapore will become the first country in the world – but almost certainly not the last – to impose a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) levy onto all flights departing the island nation.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore says the fee will apply to all flights booked from 1 October 2026, for flights departing from 1 January 2027.

Transit passengers, such as those on the Sydney-Singapore-London flights of Qantas and British Airways, will however be exempt from the charge.

Singapore’s SAF levy will vary depending on the length of the flight and the class of travel.

Band 1 – Southeast Asia: S$4 for business and first class, S$1 for premium economy and economy class

Band 2 – Northeast Asia, South Asia, Australia, Papua New Guinea: S$11.20 for business and first class, S$2.80 for premium economy and economy class

Band 3 – Africa, Central and West Asia, Europe, Middle East, Pacific Islands, New Zealand: S$25.60 for business and first class, S$6.40 for premium economy and economy class

Band 4 - Americas: S$41.60 for business and first class, S$10.40 for premium economy and economy class

This levy is based on Singapore’s goal of SAF making up 1% of fuel used for departing flight.

That target is expected to be raised to 5% by 2030, which will likely trigger an increase in the levy.

The CAAS says the money raised will go into a statutory SAF Fund used to purchase SAF and associated environmental attributes.

While several countries and airlines already chrnge a broad-based ‘green tax’ passenger levy or environmental surcharge for flights, Singapore is the first to apply a dedicated SAF levy to support the adoption of sustainable aviation fuel.
