text:
Lê Ngọc Ánh Minh - 06/09/2026

Ngành năng lượng sạch đang đứng trước một nghịch lý đau đớn: các công ty sản xuất nhiên liệu bền vững (sustainable fuels) – từ SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) cho hàng không, methanol xanh hay amoniac cho hàng hải, đến hydro cho xe tải và các ứng dụng công nghiệp – đang phá sản hàng loạt. Trong khi các chính phủ và tập đoàn lớn cam kết mạnh mẽ với lộ trình Net Zero, thì các doanh nghiệp tiên phong lại đang chết dần trên chiến trường mà họ được kỳ vọng sẽ chinh phục.

Câu hỏi đặt ra: Liệu một ngành công nghiệp chỉ tồn tại nhờ trợ cấp và chính sách có thực sự là bền vững?

Bức tranh toàn cảnh: Hàng loạt doanh nghiệp phá sản

Những con số biết nói:

SAF: Năm 2024, một trong những nhà sản xuất SAF hàng đầu thế giới, LanzaJet (có sự hậu thuẫn của các "ông lớn" như Shell, Suncor và British Airways), đã buộc phải tuyên bố phá sản chỉ vài tháng sau khi khánh thành nhà máy thương mại đầu tiên. Dù đã tiếp cận được nguồn vốn 250 triệu USD, họ vẫn không thể chịu được sự kết hợp giữa chi phí nguyên liệu tăng vọt và giá nhiên liệu hóa thạch sụt giảm . Một số dự án SAF lớn khác như Norsk e-Fuel tại Na Uy và Sasol tại Nam Phi cũng đã tạm dừng hoặc hủy bỏ các kế hoạch mở rộng.

Methanol xanh: Liquid Wind, một startup Thụy Điển với 6 dự án methanol xanh, đã nộp đơn xin phá sản. Orsted, tập đoàn năng lượng hàng đầu Đan Mạch, đã hủy bỏ dự án FlagshipONE, dự án methanol xanh lớn nhất châu Âu, thừa nhận thị trường nhiên liệu hàng hải xanh đang phát triển chậm hơn nhiều so với dự kiến, khiến dự án không khả thi về mặt kinh tế.

Hydro xanh: Năm 2023, Green Hydrogen Systems, nhà sản xuất điện phân hàng đầu Đan Mạch, đã phá sản sau nhiều năm thua lỗ và nợ nần. Nel ASA của Na Uy, một trong những công ty hydro lớn nhất thế giới, đã phải cắt giảm 20% lực lượng lao động, đình chỉ mở rộng nhà máy và nói rằng họ "không thể thực hiện đầu tư lớn" do nhu cầu mờ nhạt. Plug Power, nhà sản xuất điện phân hàng đầu Hoa Kỳ, đã phải báo động về khả năng hoạt động liên tục trong một năm tới.

Đây không phải là những cái tên nhỏ lẻ. Đó là những công ty đã nhận được hàng tỷ USD tài trợ từ chính phủ và các quỹ đầu tư. Đó là những công ty được kỳ vọng sẽ dẫn đầu cuộc cách mạng năng lượng sạch. Và họ đang thất bại.

Nghịch lý của chính sách: Trợ cấp tạo ra cầu giả tạo

Khi các chính phủ áp đặt các hạn ngạch (ví dụ: tỷ lệ SAF bắt buộc trong nhiên liệu hàng không của EU), họ đã tạo ra một "cầu bắt buộc" (mandated demand). Về mặt lý thuyết, điều này nên kích thích đầu tư và giảm chi phí theo thời gian. Nhưng thực tế:

Yêu cầu chính phủ trợ cấp: Nếu nhiên liệu bền vững không thể tự đứng vững về mặt kinh tế, các công ty sẽ không sản xuất trừ khi được trợ cấp. Nhưng trợ cấp từ ngân sách nhà nước thì có hạn và có thể bị cắt bỏ bất cứ lúc nào khi thâm hụt ngân sách hoặc chính trị thay đổi.

Chính sách thay đổi: Khi chính phủ thay đổi, chính sách có thể đảo chiều. Ví dụ, sau bầu cử Mỹ năm 2024, các quy định về khí thải và ưu đãi cho nhiên liệu bền vững đã bị đặt dấu hỏi lớn, gây ra làn sóng hoãn và hủy bỏ dự án.

Bên mua dè dặt: Các hãng hàng không, công ty vận tải biển và các nhà sản xuất ô tô, vốn đang chịu áp lực về lợi nhuận, sẵn sàng mua số lượng nhỏ để "xanh hóa" hình ảnh, nhưng từ chối ký các hợp đồng dài hạn với giá cao, khiến các dự án không thể đạt được quy mô cần thiết để giảm chi phí.

Khi giá nhiên liệu bền vững cao hơn nhiên liệu hóa thạch 3-4 lần (hoặc hơn), làm sao thị trường có thể tự vận hành? Nếu không có bên mua, hoặc bên mua chỉ mua với số lượng tối thiểu để "chứng tỏ", doanh nghiệp sản xuất sẽ không có doanh thu để trang trải chi phí vốn và vận hành khổng lồ, dẫn đến phá sản.

Bản chất của "bền vững" có phải là kinh tế?

Chúng ta đang bỏ qua một sự thật cơ bản: Tính bền vững không chỉ là màu xanh, mà còn là kinh tế. Một công nghệ, một sản phẩm hay một ngành công nghiệp chỉ thực sự bền vững khi nó có thể tồn tại và phát triển mà không cần nạng chống (trợ cấp vô hạn). Nếu giá thành quá cao, nếu công nghệ kém hiệu quả, nếu chuỗi cung ứng quá mong manh, thì dù có xanh đến đâu, nó cũng sẽ sụp đổ khi cơn gió chính trị đổi chiều.

Ngành công nghiệp nhiên liệu bền vững đang phải trả giá cho một sai lầm cơ bản: cố gắng làm điều đúng đắn nhưng bằng cách sai lầm. Họ đã tập trung vào công nghệ và chính sách, nhưng quên mất yếu tố quyết định: khách hàng. Trừ khi nhiên liệu bền vững trở nên cạnh tranh về giá với nhiên liệu hóa thạch, hoặc trừ khi một hệ thống định giá carbon toàn cầu mạnh mẽ và ổn định được áp dụng, câu chuyện phá sản sẽ tiếp tục.

Bài học cho Việt Nam và các doanh nghiệp như VH2

Đối với các nước đang phát triển như Việt Nam, bài học là rõ ràng:

Không chạy theo mốt: Đừng đầu tư vào hydro hay nhiên liệu bền vững chỉ vì đó là "xu hướng" toàn cầu, trừ khi có một chiến lược kinh tế rõ ràng.

Bắt đầu từ thị trường, không bắt đầu từ công nghệ: Trước khi xây nhà máy, hãy tìm khách hàng. Một hợp đồng mua bán dài hạn (offtake agreement) với giá có thể chấp nhận được quan trọng hơn một công nghệ tiên tiến.

Xây dựng dần dần, có lộ trình: Bắt đầu với các dự án quy mô nhỏ, gần nguồn năng lượng tái tạo và gần khách hàng tiêu thụ, nơi có thể học hỏi và tối ưu hóa mà không cần đầu tư quá mạo hiểm.

Cuộc chơi nhiên liệu bền vững không dành cho những người mơ mộng. Nó dành cho những người thực tế, những người hiểu rằng không có gì bền vững nếu nó không đứng vững về mặt kinh tế. Câu chuyện của LanzaJet, Green Hydrogen Systems, Orsted và nhiều công ty khác là một lời cảnh tỉnh đắt giá cho tất cả chúng ta.

I. So sánh giá: Nhiên liệu bền vững đắt hơn bao nhiêu?

Khoảng cách giá là rào cản lớn nhất. Dữ liệu từ các nguồn độc lập cho thấy:

Loại nhiên liệu Giá tham khảo (USD/tấn) Tỷ lệ so với nhiên liệu truyền thống Nhiên liệu hàng không truyền thống (Jet A1) ~721 - 1.404 1x (cơ sở) SAF (HEFA, Tây Bắc Âu) 2.731 - 2.830 ~2 - 3.9 lần SAF (dự báo IATA 2026) ~2.872 ~2.5 lần Nhiên liệu tàu truyền thống (VLSFO) 500 - 800 1x (cơ sở) Methanol xanh sinh học 900 - 1.400 ~1.8 - 1.9 lần Methanol xanh điện tử (e-methanol) 1.600 - 2.400 ~3.2 - 3.0 lần Diesel truyền thống ~45,09 VND/km (TCO) 1x (cơ sở) Hydro xanh cho xe tải (giá hiện tại) ~102,52 VND/km (TCO) ~2.3 lần

Báo cáo của BloombergNEF cho thấy giá SAF tại Tây Bắc Âu đã tăng 31% trong quý II/2026 do xung đột tại eo Hormuz, lên mức trung bình 2.830 USD/tấn, gấp đôi giá nhiên liệu máy bay truyền thống . IATA dự báo giá SAF năm 2026 sẽ tăng 15% lên 2.872 USD/tấn, gấp 2,5 lần nhiên liệu thông thường .

Trong lĩnh vực hàng hải, methanol xanh có thể cao gấp ba lần giá nhiên liệu tàu truyền thống, tạo ra thị trường vận tải hai tầng: các hãng tàu lớn có thể đầu tư vào các tuyến phát thải bằng không, trong khi các doanh nghiệp nhỏ hơn phải đối mặt với chi phí gia tăng và áp lực cạnh tranh .

Đối với vận tải đường bộ, phân tích tổng chi phí sở hữu (TCO) tại Ấn Độ cho thấy xe tải hydro hiện có chi phí 102,52 Rs/km, cao gấp 2,3 lần so với xe chạy diesel (45,09 Rs/km). Ngay cả khi giá hydro giảm xuống còn 200 Rs/kg, TCO vẫn chỉ gần đạt mức hòa vốn .

II. Lộ trình các chính phủ và cơ chế thị trường

Các chính phủ đang áp dụng nhiều công cụ để thúc đẩy nhiên liệu bền vững:

1. Châu Âu (EU):

ReFuelEU Aviation: Bắt buộc tỷ lệ SAF tại các sân bay EU đạt 2% (2025), 6% (2030), 70% (2050), với hạn ngạch phụ cho e-SAF (1,2% vào 2030, 35% vào 2050) .

Mức phạt không tuân thủ: Ít nhất gấp đôi chênh lệch giá SAF so với nhiên liệu truyền thống, tương đương khoảng 2.700 euro/tấn cho SAF sinh học và gần 14.000 euro/tấn cho e-kerosene tổng hợp .

Ủy ban châu Âu đã khẳng định sẽ duy trì các hạn ngạch, không thay đổi trong đợt đánh giá năm 2027 .

2. Mỹ:

Tiêu chuẩn nhiên liệu tái tạo (RVO): Yêu cầu kỷ lục 15 tỷ gallon ethanol ngô và tăng 60% lượng biodiesel và diesel tái tạo từ đậu nành so với 2025 .

Tín dụng thuế và các chương trình tín dụng carbon (LCFS) đang thúc đẩy đầu tư .

3. Nhật Bản:

Đề xuất hạn ngạch SAF áp dụng cho các chuyến bay quốc tế tại 7 sân bay lớn (chiếm 68% lượng tiếp nhiên liệu quốc tế), bắt đầu từ 1% (năm tài chính 2030-31), 3% (2031-32), 5% (2032-35). Mức này thấp hơn đáng kể so với đề xuất trước đó .

4. Hàn Quốc:

Bắt buộc giảm phát thải đối với xe tải và xe buýt hạng trung và nặng từ năm 2027, với mục tiêu giảm 30% vào 2030 so với giai đoạn 2021-2022. Các nhà sản xuất vượt chỉ tiêu sẽ nhận được tín dụng "siêu xanh" cho xe điện và hydro .

But there’s already an update to the original story: Minnesota’s new SAF blending facility at Flint Hills Resources in Rosemount is now complete, with capacity to handle up to 30 MILLION gallons of pure SAF annually and send the blended fuel directly to MSP.

For perspective, Delta alone uses about 250 million gallons of jet fuel per year at MSP. 😳

title: Inilah Cara Pertamina Kenalkan Transisi Energi Kepada Anak Muda di IdeaFest
description:
JAKARTA, NETRALNEWS.COM – Minyak jelantah yang sehari-hari dihasilkan dari rumah tangga ternyata memiliki potensi menjadi bagian dari energi masa depan. Pesan tersebut dibawa PT Pertamina (Persero) dalam gelaran IdeaFest 2026 dengan memperkenalkan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan yang salah satu bahan bakunya berasal dari Used Cooking Oil (UCO) atau minyak jelantah.
Melalui booth Pertamina di Jakarta Convention Center (JCC) Senayan, Jakarta, pengunjung diajak melihat lebih dekat perjalanan minyak jelantah, mulai dari dikumpulkan hingga dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan baku SAF. Inovasi ini sekaligus menunjukkan bagaimana partisipasi masyarakat dalam aktivitas sederhana dapat menjadi bagian dari pengembangan ekosistem energi rendah karbon.
Corporate Secretary Pertamina, Arya Dwi Paramita mengatakan, pengembangan SAF merupakan salah satu langkah konkret Pertamina dalam menjalankan transisi energi sekaligus memperkuat kemandirian energi nasional.
“Minyak itu kita buat untuk bahan bakar pesawat udara. Namun jangan khawatir, ini aman karena risetnya sudah diinisiasi sejak 2015, diteliti secara ketat dan diuji coba dari 2021 hingga 2025,” ujar Arya, Jumat (4/9/2026).
SAF berbasis minyak jelantah tersebut juga telah digunakan pada penerbangan Pelita Air Service, anak perusahaan Pertamina, untuk rute Jakarta–Bali. Pengembangan ini menjadi salah satu bukti bahwa inovasi energi rendah karbon dapat berangkat dari sumber daya yang dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari.
SAF Project Commercial PT Pertamina Patra Niaga, Ibrahim Akbar mengatakan, konsep pemanfaatan minyak jelantah menjadi salah satu topik yang paling menarik perhatian pengunjung IdeaFest.
“Hari ini saya berkesempatan mempresentasikan program Pertamina yang mengubah minyak jelantah menjadi bahan bakar terbarukan. Saya melihat antusiasme yang sangat besar. Dari semua yang bertanya, semuanya tentang UCO,” kata Ibrahim.
Menurut Ibrahim, karakter pengunjung IdeaFest yang didominasi generasi muda memberikan ruang bagi Pertamina untuk mengenalkan transisi energi dengan cara yang lebih dekat dan relevan. Tidak hanya memahami inovasinya, masyarakat juga dapat mengambil bagian melalui pengumpulan minyak jelantah sebagai bahan baku.
“Harapannya, lebih banyak lapisan masyarakat mengetahui program ini sehingga sumber bahan baku, dalam hal ini minyak jelantah, bisa kita kumpulkan sebanyak-banyaknya,” ujarnya.
Ibrahim menambahkan, pengembangan ekosistem SAF membutuhkan kolaborasi dari berbagai pihak. Selain aspek teknologi, tantangan yang perlu dijawab mencakup disparitas harga, mekanisme pengumpulan minyak jelantah, hingga dukungan regulasi. Karena itu, keterlibatan masyarakat menjadi salah satu bagian penting dalam membangun rantai pasok UCO yang lebih kuat.
“Harapan konkretnya, semakin banyak yang mengetahui program beli minyak jelantah yang sudah ada saat ini dan semakin besar jumlah atau volume minyak jelantah yang bisa kita kumpulkan,” pungkas Ibrahim.

text:
TOKYO— Japan Airlines (JAL) has acquired an undisclosed stake in Hanjin KAL, the holding company of Korean Air, marking its first known investment in a foreign airline group and setting the stage for a broader strategic partnership.

The move comes as Korean Air prepares to complete its integration with Asiana Airlines and expand its presence across the Japan–South Korea market.

Japan Airlines (JAL) and Korean Air (KE) announced the partnership in Tokyo on September 3, building on more than six decades of cooperation between the two carriers.

Advertisement

The expanded agreement will cover passenger and cargo operations, while Korea–Japan codeshare opportunities are expected to grow significantly following the Asiana integration.

JAL Expands Korean Partnership Further

The investment gives JAL a closer commercial relationship with Korean Air despite the carriers belonging to different global alliances.

Korean Air is a SkyTeam member, while JAL belongs to oneworld and maintains major transpacific cooperation with American Airlines.

The size and purchase price of JAL’s Hanjin KAL stake have not been disclosed.

JAL described the investment as an independent decision based on Hanjin KAL’s long-term market value, while industry observers have linked the timing to the shareholder contest surrounding Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae.

Hoban Group increased its Hanjin KAL holding to 20.15% in July, narrowing the gap with Cho and related parties to about 0.41 percentage points.

The development has increased attention on the company’s shareholder structure, although JAL has not publicly confirmed that its investment is intended to influence the management dispute.

Codeshare Network Expands Across Asia

The commercial focus of the new partnership will be the high-demand Japan–South Korea market.

Korean Air currently operates about 250 weekly flights on Japan routes, with the total expected to rise to roughly 400 after its December integration with Asiana Airlines.

The additional Asiana-operated Japan routes are expected to create more opportunities for codesharing and mileage cooperation between JAL and Korean Air.

The carriers already have a long-standing codeshare relationship covering routes between Japan and South Korea.

Beyond passenger services, the airlines plan to deepen cooperation in cargo operations and explore shared use of cargo terminals. They will also consider ground-handling cooperation, employee exchanges and mutual access to cabin-crew training facilities.

New Aviation Ventures Beyond Airlines

JAL and Korean Air will establish a joint task force to identify additional business opportunities outside traditional airline operations.

Areas under consideration include aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul, sustainable aviation fuel and urban air mobility.

The companies also plan to explore investment opportunities in aviation-related startups as they seek technologies and business models that can strengthen their long-term competitiveness.

The cooperation could therefore extend beyond flights and frequent-flyer programs into wider aviation services.

The strategic partnership does not mean either airline is leaving its existing global alliance. Instead, the agreement creates a separate bilateral framework that allows the carriers to cooperate while retaining their respective SkyTeam and oneworld positions, One Mile At A Time reported.

For passengers, the most visible impact is likely to come from expanded codeshare and mileage options between Japan and South Korea.

For both airlines, the partnership provides a way to capture additional passenger and cargo flows as Korean Air builds a larger network following the Asiana integration.

二氧化碳加氢制可持续航空燃料技术

Alias

CO2AF™

Definition

The thousand-ton-scale CO2 hydrogenation to Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) technology is an integrated technology developed by the Wei Fei and Zhang Chenxi team at Tsinghua University , which directly converts industrially captured carbon dioxide and green hydrogen into Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) through catalytic reactions. In August 2026, the technology passed the scientific and technological achievement evaluation organized by the China Petroleum and Chemical Industry Federation , and was recognized by the evaluation committee led by Academician He Mingyuan as "a world first, with the overall technology at the world-leading level."

1

Its core technical route is a "one-step process" synthesis, employing the independently developed nano spinel-molecular sieve bifunctional coupled catalyst to achieve targeted and efficient conversion from CO₂ to jet fuel components in a single reactor.

1

This technology belongs to the non-biomass route, opening up a new near-zero carbon cycle path of "industrial waste gas—green jet fuel." Its raw material supply is not limited by biomass resources, providing a brand-new solution for the large-scale production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel.

1

Development History

In response to the dual carbon strategy and energy security challenges, and to break the dependence of traditional sustainable aviation fuel on biomass feedstocks, the technology was developed through joint research by multiple institutions, led by the Wei Fei and Zhang Chenxi team at Tsinghua University .

1

The world's first thousand-tonne pilot plant was built in Meishan, Sichuan. As of August 2026, it had accumulated more than 2,000 hours of safe and stable operation.

1

From August 11 to 14, 2026, the pilot plant passed a 72-hour continuous full-load on-site assessment.

2

On August 17, 2026, the technology passed the scientific and technological achievement evaluation organized by the China Petroleum and Chemical Industry Federation and was recognized by the evaluation committee as “a world first, with the overall technology at the world-leading level”.

1

The successful evaluation of the thousand-tonne pilot plant marks that the technology has met the conditions for industrial scale-up, and the preliminary work for the 10,000-tonne-class industrial demonstration unit has been fully launched.

1

Applications

The core engineering validation case of this technology is a thousand-tonne-scale pilot plant for the production of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) via CO2 hydrogenation, located in Sichuan Meishan High-tech Industrial Park. The plant was jointly constructed and operated by the Wei Fei and Zhang Chenxi team of Tsinghua University , together with Sichuan Golden Elephant Sairui Chemical Co., Ltd. and other organizations. It has accumulated more than 2,000 hours of stable operation and, in August 2026, passed a continuous 72-hour full-load on-site assessment and a scientific and technological achievement evaluation organized by the China Petroleum and Chemical Industry Federation .

2

The results of the on-site assessment and calibration showed that the plant ran steadily at full load: total carbon dioxide conversion reached 97.37%, the selectivity of the C₈⁺ jet fuel fraction was 92.37%, and methane selectivity was 1.67%. Producing each tonne of jet fuel fraction consumed 3.65 tonnes of carbon dioxide and 5,020 standard cubic meters of hydrogen. Catalyst performance and process parameters met and exceeded design expectations.

1

All indicators of the jet fuel fraction produced by the plant comply with the national standard GB 6537-2025 No. 3 Jet Fuel, and the product has been tested by the CAAC Testing Center and multiple other institutions. Its quality meets and exceeds the requirements of the national standard.

1

Based on the pilot test results, this technology has met the conditions for industrial scale-up and provides a technical route for the large-scale production of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Subsequently, technical optimization and engineering verification will be carried out in connection with the construction of a 10,000-tonne-scale industrial demonstration plant.

1

Related Derivatives

This technology is called "CO2 Hydrogenation to Sustainable Aviation Fuel Technology", and its technical solution is also known as CO2AF™. The core innovations of this technology include catalyst innovation, reaction engineering innovation, and process integration innovation. In catalyst innovation, a multi-active-site "catalytic split-flow" strategy was adopted to create a nano spinel-molecular sieve bifunctional coupled catalyst. In reaction engineering innovation, a phase diagram of pressure-induced gas-solid multiphase fluidization was constructed, enabling the independent design, manufacture, and stable operation of a high-pressure hydrogenation fluidized-bed reactor. In process integration innovation, a complete set of technologies for the direct production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel through carbon dioxide hydrogenation has been developed, achieving a one-step leap from carbon dioxide to jet fuel components with highly directional conversion and low hydrogen consumption.

1

Compared with traditional Sustainable Aviation Fuel production technologies that rely on biomass feedstocks such as animal and vegetable oils, this technology uses industrially captured carbon dioxide and green hydrogen as raw materials, and features a wide range of feedstock sources, no competition with people for grain, and no competition with grain for land.

1

In August 2026, this technology passed the scientific and technological achievement evaluation organized by the China Petroleum and Chemical Industry Federation. The key assessment data for the thousand-tonne pilot plant were as follows: total conversion of carbon dioxide reached 97.37%, jet fuel component selectivity was 92.37%, and the product complied with the GB 6537-2025 No. 3 Jet Fuel standard.

1

With this technology, the world's first thousand-tonne pilot plant has been built in Meishan, Sichuan, and has been in stable operation for over 2,000 hours in total. The preparatory work for the 10,000-tonne-class industrial demonstration unit has been fully launched.

text:
JAKARTA, Investortrust.id - PT Pertamina (Persero), memperkenalkan pemanfaatan minyak jelantah (used cooking oil/UCO) sebagai salah satu bahan baku sustainable aviation fuel atau SAF dalam gelaran IdeaFest 2026 di Jakarta Convention Center, Jakarta. Inovasi tersebut membuka peluang bagi limbah minyak rumah tangga untuk masuk ke rantai pasok bahan bakar penerbangan rendah karbon.

Melalui booth Pertamina, pengunjung melihat perjalanan minyak jelantah dari proses pengumpulan hingga pemanfaatannya sebagai bahan baku SAF. Pengembangan tersebut juga memperlihatkan peran masyarakat dalam menyediakan bahan baku untuk mendukung transisi energi.

Corporate Secretary Pertamina Arya Dwi Paramita mengatakan pengembangan SAF menjadi salah satu langkah konkret perseroan dalam menjalankan transisi energi sekaligus memperkuat kemandirian energi nasional.

“Minyak itu kita buat untuk bahan bakar pesawat udara. Namun jangan khawatir, ini aman karena risetnya sudah diinisiasi sejak 2015, diteliti secara ketat dan diuji coba dari 2021 hingga 2025,” ujar Arya, dikutip Minggu (6/9/2026).

Menurut Arya, pengembangan bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan tersebut telah melalui rangkaian penelitian dan pengujian dalam beberapa tahun. Proses tersebut dilakukan sebelum SAF berbasis minyak jelantah digunakan dalam penerbangan komersial.

SAF berbasis minyak jelantah tersebut juga telah digunakan pada penerbangan Pelita Air Service, anak perusahaan Pertamina, untuk rute Jakarta-Bali. Pemanfaatan itu menjadi bagian dari pengembangan penggunaan bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan di sektor aviasi nasional.

Teken Enam Kesepakatan, Pertamina NRE Dorong Pengembangan Biofuel hingga Hidrogen

Kehadiran teknologi tersebut di IdeaFest juga membawa pesan bahwa pengembangan energi rendah karbon tidak hanya berkaitan dengan teknologi berskala besar. Bahan yang selama ini dianggap sebagai limbah rumah tangga juga dapat memiliki nilai ekonomi ketika dikumpulkan dan dikelola melalui rantai pasok yang tepat.

SAF Project Commercial PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Ibrahim Akbar mengatakan pemanfaatan minyak jelantah menjadi salah satu topik yang mendapat perhatian besar dari pengunjung IdeaFest 2026. “Saya melihat antusiasme yang sangat besar. Dari semua yang bertanya, semuanya tentang UCO,” kata Ibrahim.

Ibrahim mengatakan karakter pengunjung IdeaFest yang banyak berasal dari generasi muda memberikan ruang bagi Pertamina untuk memperkenalkan isu transisi energi dengan pendekatan yang lebih dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari.

Menurut dia, masyarakat tidak hanya dapat mengenal teknologi yang digunakan dalam pengembangan SAF. Masyarakat juga dapat berkontribusi secara langsung dengan mengumpulkan minyak jelantah untuk kemudian masuk ke dalam rantai pasok bahan baku.

“Harapannya, lebih banyak lapisan masyarakat mengetahui program ini sehingga sumber bahan baku, dalam hal ini minyak jelantah, bisa kita kumpulkan sebanyak-banyaknya,” ujarnya.

Pengumpulan UCO menjadi salah satu aspek penting karena ketersediaan bahan baku turut menentukan kemampuan pengembangan SAF dalam skala yang lebih besar. Semakin banyak minyak jelantah yang dapat dikumpulkan melalui mekanisme yang terorganisasi, semakin besar pula potensi pasokan bahan baku yang tersedia.

Tantangan Pengembangan SAF

Ibrahim mengatakan pengembangan ekosistem SAF tidak hanya membutuhkan kesiapan teknologi. Pertamina juga menghadapi sejumlah tantangan, mulai dari perbedaan harga, mekanisme pengumpulan minyak jelantah hingga dukungan regulasi.

Perbedaan harga menjadi salah satu aspek yang perlu diperhatikan karena SAF harus dapat dikembangkan dalam ekosistem yang mampu mendukung keberlanjutan bisnis. Pada saat yang sama, mekanisme pengumpulan UCO perlu dibangun agar pasokan bahan baku dapat tersedia secara konsisten.

Dukungan regulasi juga menjadi bagian penting dalam pengembangan industri tersebut. Kolaborasi antara pelaku usaha, pemerintah dan masyarakat dibutuhkan untuk membentuk rantai pasok UCO yang lebih kuat.

“Harapan konkretnya, semakin banyak yang mengetahui program beli minyak jelantah yang sudah ada saat ini dan semakin besar jumlah atau volume minyak jelantah yang bisa kita kumpulkan,” pungkas Ibrahim.

Arya mengatakan Pertamina memiliki peran strategis dalam menjaga ketersediaan energi nasional. Namun, kebutuhan energi Indonesia masih lebih besar dibandingkan kemampuan produksi dalam negeri sehingga sebagian pasokan harus dipenuhi melalui impor.

Melalui dual growth strategy, Pertamina menjalankan dua fokus secara bersamaan. Perusahaan tetap mengoptimalkan bisnis energi yang sudah berjalan untuk memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat, sementara bisnis rendah karbon dan energi baru terbarukan terus dikembangkan sebagai sumber pertumbuhan berikutnya.

Salah satu inovasi yang dikembangkan Pertamina adalah pemanfaatan used cooking oil (UCO), yakni minyak jelantah, sebagai bahan baku SAF. Minyak jelantah yang telah dikumpulkan kemudian diproses di Kilang Pertamina Cilacap bersama bahan baku pendukung lainnya untuk menghasilkan bahan bakar penerbangan rendah karbon.

“Minyak itu kita buat untuk bahan bakar pesawat udara. Namun jangan khawatir, ini aman karena risetnya sudah diinisiasi sejak 2015, diteliti secara ketat dan diuji coba dari 2021 hingga 2025,” kata Arya.

Arya mengatakan pendekatan tersebut menjadi bagian dari strategi perusahaan dalam menghadapi perubahan sistem energi. Pertamina tidak serta-merta meninggalkan sumber energi yang saat ini masih menjadi kebutuhan utama masyarakat, tetapi secara bersamaan mulai membangun portofolio energi yang lebih rendah karbon.

text:
Henan Junheng Industrial Group Biotechnology Co., Ltd., based in Henan Province in central China, is producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from waste cooking oil at industrial scale, using a multi-stage conversion process that transforms used cooking oil into bio-jet fuel chemically identical to conventional aviation kerosene.

At the facility, waste oils first undergo multiple pretreatment steps to reduce levels of metal, phosphorus, chlorine, nitrogen, and other impurities, yielding purified, industrial-grade mixed oil. The oil then enters a hydrodeoxygenation reactor, where a proprietary catalyst breaks down and reassembles oil molecules to produce bio-jet fuel that is fully compatible with existing aircraft engines and requires no engine modifications.

Du Zhisheng, a researcher in the company's technical department, said the team developed a catalyst system resistant to both acid and water, describing it as acting "like a 'gluttonous snake'" that devours metals in the oil while converting it into aviation fuel. The company said bio-based aviation fuel reduces carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 80 percent over its entire life cycle compared to conventional jet fuel.

title: Agrinas Palma Dorong Peningkatan Produktivitas Sawit untuk Dukung Bioenergi Nasional
description:
Agrinas Palma Nusantara menilai peningkatan produktivitas perkebunan kelapa sawit menjadi kunci untuk menjaga pasokan bahan baku yang berkelanjutan.
Direktur Utama Agrinas Palma Nusantara Mohammad Abdul Ghani mengatakan bahwa pengembangan bioenergi tidak cukup hanya mengandalkan kebijakan mandatori di sektor hilir, melainkan perlu dukungan sektor agroindustri yang menyediakan bahan baku secara konsisten.
Untuk itu, produktivitas sawit harus meningkat dari sekitar 3 ton menjadi 4,4 ton CPO per hektare, dengan tambahan areal sekitar 7,4 juta hektare.
Agrinas Palma juga mengembangkan bioetanol terintegrasi berbasis singkong yang menghubungkan perkebunan 4.000–6.000 hektare dengan pabrik kapasitas 100 kiloliter per hari.
Pengembangan biodiesel dan bioetanol ini direncanakan melalui kerja sama Agrinas Palma dan Pertamina dengan dukungan Danantara, di mana Agrinas Palma mengelola lahan dan rantai pasok bahan baku, sementara Pertamina membangun dan mengoperasikan pabrik serta menjadi pembeli produk.
text:
Pengembangan industri bioenergi nasional menghadapi tantangan ketersediaan bahan baku karena kebutuhan biodiesel, pangan, ekspor, produk turunan, dan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) terus meningkat, dilansir dari Ekonomi.

Agrinas Palma Nusantara menilai peningkatan produktivitas perkebunan kelapa sawit menjadi kunci untuk menjaga pasokan bahan baku yang berkelanjutan.

Direktur Utama Agrinas Palma Nusantara Mohammad Abdul Ghani mengatakan bahwa pengembangan bioenergi tidak cukup hanya mengandalkan kebijakan mandatori di sektor hilir, melainkan perlu dukungan sektor agroindustri yang menyediakan bahan baku secara konsisten.

"Indonesia memiliki potensi bioenergi yang sangat besar. Tantangannya adalah bagaimana meningkatkan produktivitas, menjaga keberlanjutan, serta memastikan hasil dari sektor hulu dapat terhubung dengan kebutuhan industri bioenergi nasional," ujar Mohammad Abdul Ghani, Jumat (4/9/2026).

Berdasarkan analisis data Agrinas Palma, kebutuhan minyak sawit mentah (CPO) Indonesia diperkirakan mencapai 104 juta ton pada 2045 untuk memenuhi biodiesel, pangan, ekspor, produk turunan, dan SAF.

Untuk itu, produktivitas sawit harus meningkat dari sekitar 3 ton menjadi 4,4 ton CPO per hektare, dengan tambahan areal sekitar 7,4 juta hektare.

Tantangan lain datang dari perkebunan sawit rakyat yang mencapai 42% dari total luas sawit nasional atau 6,94 juta hektare, di mana 2,8 juta hektarenya berusia lebih dari 25 tahun dan melibatkan 1,4 juta keluarga.

Produktivitas sawit rakyat yang rendah, sekitar 2,6 ton CPO per hektare, disebabkan tanaman tua dan rendahnya realisasi Peremajaan Sawit Rakyat (PSR).

Agrinas Palma menyatakan produktivitas ini masih bisa ditingkatkan hingga sekitar 5 ton CPO per hektare dengan praktik budidaya baik, tetapi realisasi PSR baru mencapai 20.000 hektare per tahun dengan alokasi dana kurang dari 5% pada 2021–2023.

Perusahaan menilai percepatan PSR, pola tumpang sari tanaman pangan, praktik pertanian baik, digitalisasi, mekanisasi, serta riset dan inovasi harus menjadi fokus peningkatan produktivitas.

Di hilir, CPO dan produk samping pengolahan sawit dapat menjadi bahan baku berbagai produk energi seperti biodiesel, green diesel, SAF, biogas, dan bahan bakar co-firing.

Agrinas Palma juga mengembangkan bioetanol terintegrasi berbasis singkong yang menghubungkan perkebunan 4.000–6.000 hektare dengan pabrik kapasitas 100 kiloliter per hari.

Kebutuhan bahan baku diperkirakan sekitar 200.000 ton singkong per tahun untuk menghasilkan 30.000 kiloliter bioetanol, dengan produk samping mendukung peternakan sapi terintegrasi.

Pengembangan biodiesel dan bioetanol ini direncanakan melalui kerja sama Agrinas Palma dan Pertamina dengan dukungan Danantara, di mana Agrinas Palma mengelola lahan dan rantai pasok bahan baku, sementara Pertamina membangun dan mengoperasikan pabrik serta menjadi pembeli produk.

"Kami ingin menghasilkan biodiesel dan bioetanol dengan dukungan pasokan bahan baku dari sektor agroindustri nasional. Untuk mewujudkannya, diperlukan kolaborasi antara pemerintah, BUMN, pelaku industri, lembaga pembiayaan, serta pemilik teknologi," ujarnya.

text:
Jakarta: Minyak jelantah yang sehari-hari dihasilkan dari rumah tangga ternyata memiliki potensi menjadi bagian dari energi masa depan. Pesan tersebut dibawa PT Pertamina (Persero) dalam gelaran IdeaFest 2026 dengan memperkenalkan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan yang salah satu bahan bakunya berasal dari Used Cooking Oil (UCO) atau minyak jelantah.

Melalui booth Pertamina di Jakarta Convention Center (JCC) Senayan, Jakarta, pengunjung diajak melihat lebih dekat perjalanan minyak jelantah, mulai dari dikumpulkan hingga dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan baku SAF. Inovasi ini sekaligus menunjukkan bagaimana partisipasi masyarakat dalam aktivitas sederhana dapat menjadi bagian dari pengembangan ekosistem energi rendah karbon.

SAF Project Commercial PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Ibrahim Akbar salah satu pembicara di booth Pertamina dalam acara Ideafest 2026 yang diselenggarakan di Jakarta International Convention Center (JICC), pada Jumat, 4 September 2026. (Dok. Pertamina)

Corporate Secretary Pertamina, Arya Dwi Paramita mengatakan, pengembangan SAF merupakan salah satu langkah konkret Pertamina dalam menjalankan transisi energi sekaligus memperkuat kemandirian energi nasional.

“Minyak itu kita buat untuk bahan bakar pesawat udara. Namun jangan khawatir, ini aman karena risetnya sudah diinisiasi sejak 2015, diteliti secara ketat dan diuji coba dari 2021 hingga 2025,” ujar Arya, Jumat, 4 September 2026.

SAF berbasis minyak jelantah tersebut juga telah digunakan pada penerbangan Pelita Air Service, anak perusahaan Pertamina, untuk rute Jakarta–Bali. Pengembangan ini menjadi salah satu bukti bahwa inovasi energi rendah karbon dapat berangkat dari sumber daya yang dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari.

SAF Project Commercial PT Pertamina Patra Niaga, Ibrahim Akbar mengatakan, konsep pemanfaatan minyak jelantah menjadi salah satu topik yang paling menarik perhatian pengunjung IdeaFest.

“Hari ini saya berkesempatan mempresentasikan program Pertamina yang mengubah minyak jelantah menjadi bahan bakar terbarukan. Saya melihat antusiasme yang sangat besar. Dari semua yang bertanya, semuanya tentang UCO,” kata Ibrahim.

Menurut Ibrahim, karakter pengunjung IdeaFest yang didominasi generasi muda memberikan ruang bagi Pertamina untuk mengenalkan transisi energi dengan cara yang lebih dekat dan relevan. Tidak hanya memahami inovasinya, masyarakat juga dapat mengambil bagian melalui pengumpulan minyak jelantah sebagai bahan baku.

“Harapannya, lebih banyak lapisan masyarakat mengetahui program ini sehingga sumber bahan baku, dalam hal ini minyak jelantah, bisa kita kumpulkan sebanyak-banyaknya,” ujarnya.

Ibrahim menambahkan, pengembangan ekosistem SAF membutuhkan kolaborasi dari berbagai pihak. Selain aspek teknologi, tantangan yang perlu dijawab mencakup disparitas harga, mekanisme pengumpulan minyak jelantah, hingga dukungan regulasi. Karena itu, keterlibatan masyarakat menjadi salah satu bagian penting dalam membangun rantai pasok UCO yang lebih kuat.

“Harapan konkretnya, semakin banyak yang mengetahui program beli minyak jelantah yang sudah ada saat ini dan semakin besar jumlah atau volume minyak jelantah yang bisa kita kumpulkan,” pungkas Ibrahim.

title: Denmark Is Transforming Sustainable Travel As New Green City Rewards Unlock Better ...
description:
Denmark is changing Sustainable Travel through Copenhagen’s visitor reward model, first tested in 2024 and expanded during summer 2025.
The programme’s confirmed scope covers Sustainable Travel, local experiences and responsible destination planning.
Sustainable Travel Gains Support From Wider European Tourism Policies Copenhagen’s reward programme forms part of a broader change in European destination management.
Together, these initiatives show how Sustainable Travel is being connected with technology, public infrastructure, environmental management and resident wellbeing.
What Happens Next for Sustainable Travel Across Europe Europe has combined its former smart tourism capital and green pioneer competitions under the European Capitals of Tourism identity.
text:
Denmark is changing Sustainable Travel through Copenhagen’s visitor reward model, first tested in 2024 and expanded during summer 2025. The initiative offered selected benefits to visitors who cycled, used public transport, arrived by train, stayed longer or joined environmental activities. Official findings recorded higher bicycle rentals and strong participant satisfaction. The development matters because European cities are seeking practical ways to manage tourism without concentrating solely on visitor growth. Travellers can access optional experiences through qualifying actions. However, the programme creates no visa privileges, passport exemptions, border benefits or changes to existing immigration requirements.

Verified Evidence Defines the Real Scope of the Tourism Development

The central story concerns destination management, responsible visitor behaviour and European tourism policy. Transport and seasonality provide important supporting context. Visa and passport matters represent only a small part of the report because no related immigration change has occurred. The percentages below are an editorial assessment based on the amount, relevance and strength of verified evidence. They are not government statistics or measurements of economic impact.

The verified evidence confirms that Copenhagen tested a voluntary tourism incentive and later increased its scale. It also establishes that European authorities are supporting greener, accessible and digitally managed destinations. The evidence does not prove that rewards reduced total citywide emissions, accommodation prices or visitor congestion. It also does not establish changes in international demand. The programme’s confirmed scope covers Sustainable Travel, local experiences and responsible destination planning.

Copenhagen Expanded Its Rewards After a Successful Initial Trial

Copenhagen introduced CopenPay through a four-week pilot during 2024. Visitors could complete approved actions and receive selected cultural or recreational experiences. Qualifying activities included cycling, using public transport, collecting litter and participating in environmental work. Official results showed that bicycle rentals connected with the initiative increased by 29%. Several tonnes of litter were also collected, although the published summary did not provide one consolidated weight. Participant satisfaction reached 98%, showing that visitors were willing to engage with Sustainable Travel through practical actions.

The programme returned between 17 June and 17 August 2025. It was three times larger than the original trial and involved more than 100 participating attractions and experiences. Eligibility expanded to include travellers arriving by train, using electric vehicles, purchasing sustainable aviation fuel or staying for four nights or longer. Available benefits included bicycle rental, guided visits, attraction access, vegetarian meals and wellbeing activities. Bicycle rentals increased by 59% during this edition. Afterwards, 70% of participants said they intended to maintain responsible habits at home, while the satisfaction rate remained at 98%.

Sustainable Travel Gains Support From Wider European Tourism Policies

Copenhagen’s reward programme forms part of a broader change in European destination management. The European tourism transition framework was published on 4 February 2022 after discussions with authorities and tourism stakeholders. It identified 27 action areas supporting environmental improvement, digitalisation and economic resilience. These areas cover governance, transport, energy, workforce skills, data, accessibility and tourism services. The policy does not force cities to adopt identical rewards. It provides a common structure through which destinations can develop measures suited to their pressures and infrastructure.

European tourism competitions have reinforced this direction. Tampere in Finland and Dubrovnik in Croatia received the two European smart tourism titles for 2026. A European jury selected the cities in November 2025, before their title-year programmes began in March 2026. Tampere received recognition for digital services, accessibility, cultural heritage and responsible growth. Dubrovnik gained recognition for addressing intense visitor pressure around its historic centre. Together, these initiatives show how Sustainable Travel is being connected with technology, public infrastructure, environmental management and resident wellbeing.

Official Figures Reveal the Scale of Europes Seasonal Challenge

European tourism remains heavily concentrated during summer. Official accommodation figures show that July and August generated 31.1% of all nights spent in European Union tourist establishments during 2025. August recorded 3.6 times more overnight stays than January. Croatia experienced the strongest concentration, with 54.5% of its annual nights occurring during those two months. Bulgaria recorded 43.4%, while Greece reached 41.6%. Malta had the lowest measured share at 21.9%, followed by Germany at 24% and Finland at 24.1%.

Short-stay accommodation booked through major online platforms generated 951.6 million guest nights across the European Union during 2025. That total was 11.4% higher than in 2024. The platform figure cannot be added directly to conventional accommodation totals because some properties may appear in both reporting systems. Nevertheless, the data illustrates the scale of demand that destinations must manage. Sustainable Travel initiatives, off-season trips and longer stays could distribute demand more evenly, although further evidence is needed before presenting that outcome as proven.

How Tourism Rewards Could Affect Visitors and Local Communities

The immediate benefit for travellers is access to selected discounts, complimentary admission or local experiences. Participating attractions can encourage visitors to reach them by bicycle or public transport. Hotels may also connect longer stays with responsible tourism packages. Local businesses outside established landmark areas could receive additional spending when programmes guide visitors towards less familiar neighbourhoods. However, no official data confirms that the Copenhagen initiative increased overall visitor arrivals, tourism expenditure or hotel occupancy.

Tourism dispersal also creates challenges. Moving visitors beyond heavily visited districts can distribute income, but it may transfer congestion into residential areas. Cycling cannot serve every visitor, making accessible alternatives essential. Rewards also require funding, participating venues and reliable verification systems. Environmental claims need comparable measurements covering transport emissions, energy, water, waste and community attitudes. Awards and certifications may strengthen destination credibility, but they do not prove that every operator follows the same standards. Effective Sustainable Travel therefore depends on transparent evidence rather than promotional claims alone.

Practical Information for Visitors Considering Rewarded Activities

Participation in Copenhagen’s programme remains voluntary. Travellers do not need to change confirmed European travel plans because of these initiatives. Anyone interested in receiving a benefit should verify whether the programme operates during the intended visit. Offers may have limited capacity, fixed dates or individual conditions. An attraction may also require advance booking or evidence of the completed action.

Travellers should consider these practical steps:

Confirm the programme’s current operating dates.

Check which visitor actions qualify for rewards.

Read the proof and redemption requirements.

Determine whether advance booking is necessary.

Confirm whether the offer provides free admission or a discount.

Review opening hours, age limits and accessibility information.

Retain rail tickets, accommodation records and relevant receipts.

Consult official public transport information before travelling.

Check regular passport and visa requirements separately.

Do not assume that participation provides immigration benefits.

No European authority has announced a passport or visa change connected with these programmes. CopenPay does not provide entry permission, priority border processing or exemptions from Schengen rules. Travellers must continue following requirements based on their nationality, destination and intended length of stay. The rewards affect activities within the destination, not permission to enter it.

What Happens Next for Sustainable Travel Across Europe

Europe has combined its former smart tourism capital and green pioneer competitions under the European Capitals of Tourism identity. The rules and prizes remain unchanged. One category covers cities with more than 100,000 residents and assesses sustainability, accessibility, digitalisation, heritage and creativity. The second normally covers destinations with populations between 25,000 and 100,000 and focuses on green-transition practices. Applications for the 2027 awards closed on 12 June 2026. Four shortlisted cities are due to be announced in September, followed by the selection of two winners in November 2026.

text:
Sustainability LIVE: The London Summit + Awards returns to London on 8–9 September 2026, bringing more than 1,000 sustainability professionals together at the QEII Centre in Westminster.

The two-day hybrid conference is designed to help senior leaders accelerate the sustainability transition by turning climate and ESG ambitions into business action.

With more than 50 expert speakers, 10 core content themes and four interactive workshops, the programme will explore how organisations can address the challenges slowing progress.

Sessions will examine climate disclosure, circular economy models, innovation and stakeholder engagement, giving attendees practical perspectives to support sustainability strategies.

Bringing together sustainability executives, business leaders and solution providers creates a space to share approaches, identify opportunities and consider how organisations can move from commitments to measurable progress.

Connecting sustainability across business

Accelerating the sustainability transition requires action across the organisation rather than within sustainability teams alone.

Co-located with Procurement & Supply Chain LIVE: The London Summit + Awards, the event connects sustainability leaders with procurement and supply chain professionals working on many of the same challenges.

This cross-functional approach can help businesses align climate targets with sourcing, procurement, supplier engagement and operational strategies.

Attendees can explore how sustainability can become part of everyday business decisions, helping organisations identify where changes can deliver environmental and commercial value.

The event also creates opportunities to learn from peers and compare approaches to implementing sustainability programmes at scale.

By bringing different functions together, Sustainability LIVE provides a setting for businesses to consider how collaboration can accelerate progress across their operations and value chains.

Sponsors supporting business transformation

The event's sponsors and partners bring expertise across the technologies, services and strategies that businesses can use to accelerate their sustainability transition.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is working to develop more sustainable cloud infrastructure, focusing on efficiency and reducing environmental impact while helping customers pursue their sustainability goals.

EcoVadis provides sustainability intelligence, ratings, risk and carbon management tools and e-learning, helping businesses assess performance and improve sustainability across their value chains, with more than 150,000 businesses using its solutions across 185 countries.

Experian brings data, analytics and technology capabilities that can help organisations gain deeper insights across sectors including financial services, healthcare, automotive and insurance, supported by a workforce of 25,200 people across 33 countries.

Sedex helps businesses map, assess, identify and mitigate supply chain risks, supporting sustainability and resilience across a community of 90,000 businesses and 104,000 supply chain sites in 35 sectors.

veritree focuses on the restorative economy, providing traceability and impact measurement for nature-based solutions and connecting businesses with verified environmental and social action, with 150 million trees pledged through its platform.

At Sustainability LIVE: The Leadership Summit in London this June, veritree CEO and Co-Founder Derrick Emsley talked about how hard it is to scale reliable nature-based solutions.

"Nature itself is an incredibly hard, challenging place to work," Derrick says.

"It's not as easy as just a checkbox. In a lot of cases, organisations want to invest in nature, but they don't understand how. And what you see a lot is groups looking for either the input — the tree being planted — or the outcome, which may be carbon or biodiversity.

“But connecting those two dots is where a lot of these projects tend to fail. You might fund the tree planting, but you're not funding the actual healthy forest at the end of it. Or you're trying to fund the carbon impact, but you're not actually funding the appropriate inputs and steps in the journey to get there.

“Then five years in, you realise the impact wasn't actually there.

"Nature itself is a long-term investment. It's about connecting the inputs within those projects to the actual tangible outcomes and monitoring that journey through the entire project.

“That, to us, is what makes a high-quality, high-integrity nature-based project."

Datamaran uses AI to provide continuous intelligence on sustainability risks, regulations, stakeholder needs and peer actions, helping corporate leaders anticipate change and identify risks and opportunities.

Neste brings expertise in renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, with renewable production capacity expected to reach 6.8 million tonnes annually in 2027 as it focuses on renewable fuels that can help customers reduce GHG emissions.

Project Management Institute (PMI) supports organisations and project professionals with knowledge, resources and certifications designed to help deliver projects and transformations effectively and responsibly.

Platinum sponsors SGS United Kingdom Ltd, Watershed and Business Stream add further expertise, spanning sustainability assurance, climate and ESG data, decarbonisation, water efficiency and water management.

Together, the sponsor community reflects the different capabilities businesses need to accelerate the transition – from measuring and managing sustainability performance to transforming supply chains, deploying technology, reducing emissions and delivering projects.

Turn insight into sustainability action

Sustainability LIVE is designed to give business leaders the opportunity to connect insight with action as organisations face growing pressure to accelerate their sustainability transition.

title: El proyecto pionero Eco2fly avanza en su planificación para descarbonizar las industrias de ... - ABC
description:
El proyecto contempla la construcción de nuevas instalaciones junto a la planta cementera que Holcim tiene en Villaluenga de la Sagra (Toledo), donde se llevará a cabo la producción de este combustible sintético para aviación.
Ahora la novedad y avance en este interesante proyecto viene dado por el acuerdo alcanzado entre Volotea, la aerolínea de las pequeñas y medianas ciudades europeas, y Eco2fly.
Hay que tener en cuenta que Volotea ya ha avanzado en la incorporación de combustibles sostenibles de aviación en sus operaciones.
En el caso de Eco2fly, el proyecto está diseñado para la creación de una cadena de valor integrada para la producción de eSAF en España.
Eco2fly reúne capacidades industriales, energéticas y logísticas complementarias, gracias a la participación de Holcim, Eco2fly Power y Exolum, para producir en Europa los combustibles que necesita nuestra aviación.
text:
La iniciativa energética está impulsada y desarrollada por Holcim, Eco2fly Power y Exolum, que trabajan conjuntamente en el desarrollo de una solución destinada a contribuir a la reducción de las emisiones de carbono de dos sectores estratégicos como son la industria cementera y la aviación.

El proyecto contempla la construcción de nuevas instalaciones junto a la planta cementera que Holcim tiene en Villaluenga de la Sagra (Toledo), donde se llevará a cabo la producción de este combustible sintético para aviación. La puesta en marcha de estas instalaciones está prevista para 2032.

Tal y como ya informó ABC, se trata de un innovador proyecto de economía circular en CO2 que transformará las emisiones industriales, que son inherentes al proceso de producción de cemento, en combustible sostenible para la aviación, formando una simbiosis entre ambos. Esta energía puede sustituir directamente al queroseno convencional, de origen fósil, sin necesidad de adaptaciones en las aeronaves ni en la infraestructura de abastecimiento, facilitando así la descarbonización inmediata del transporte aéreo.

Con esta iniciativa se prevé capturar alrededor de 700.000 toneladas de CO₂ generadas en la planta de cemento que Holcim tiene en la localidad toledana de Villaluenga de la Sagra, una de las mayores de España, y transformar la mitad de ese CO₂ en combustible e-SAF de calidad aeronáutica, suficiente para cubrir la mayor parte de la demanda de España en 2031, mientras que el CO₂ restante se almacenará de forma permanente en formaciones geológicas. Parte de ese CO2 será combinado con hidrógeno verde, producido a partir de energía renovable, para convertirlo en combustible sostenible de aviación (e-SAF), alcanzando una producción estimada de 100.000 toneladas anuales.

Ahora la novedad y avance en este interesante proyecto viene dado por el acuerdo alcanzado entre Volotea, la aerolínea de las pequeñas y medianas ciudades europeas, y Eco2fly. Se trata de la firma de un memorando de entendimiento (MoU) para explorar el suministro futuro de eSAF y que refuerza el compromiso de las partes con la descarbonización del transporte aéreo, así como con el desarrollo de una cadena de valor europea para combustibles sostenibles.

Según han informado a este periódico las empresas que acometen este proyecto, el acuerdo «contribuye a avanzar en la senda marcada por ReFuelEU Aviation, el reglamento europeo destinado a impulsar el uso de combustibles sostenibles en la aviación y a reducir la huella ambiental del transporte aéreo, y refuerza el compromiso de Volotea de alcanzar las cero emisiones netas en 2050». A este respecto, hay que tener en cuenta que la normativa establece una incorporación progresiva de SAF en los vuelos con origen en aeropuertos de la Unión Europea: un 2% entre 2025 y 2030; un 6% entre 2030 y 2035, incluyendo un 1,2% de eSAF; y hasta un 70% en 2050.

Las promotoras de esta alianza estratégica indican también que «esta iniciativa conjunta contempla un periodo de suministro de eSAF de diez años desde el inicio comercial de la planta de Eco2Fly, previsto para 2032. Los volúmenes previstos se incorporarán de forma progresiva: 6,5 millones de litros en 2032; entre 12 y 19 millones de litros en 2033 y 2034; y 32 millones litros a partir de 2035».

Hay que tener en cuenta que Volotea ya ha avanzado en la incorporación de combustibles sostenibles de aviación en sus operaciones. En 2025, la compañía utilizó más de siete millones de litros de SAF en sus vuelos, lo que representó el 2,02% de su consumo total de combustible, más de tres veces por encima del promedio estimado de la industria aeronáutica para ese año, situado en el 0,6% de la demanda total de combustible jet. Los SAF utilizados por Volotea permiten reducir alrededor de un 90% las emisiones de CO₂ a lo largo de su ciclo de vida en comparación con el combustible jet fósil actual.

El eSAF (electro Sustainable Aviation Fuel) es un combustible sintético producido a partir de hidrógeno renovable y CO₂ que permite reducir más de un 75% las emisiones netas de gases de efecto invernadero respecto al queroseno fósil convencional. A diferencia de

otros combustibles sostenibles de aviación basados en materias primas biogénicas, el eSAF utiliza electricidad renovable, agua y CO₂ como principales insumos, lo que reduce la dependencia de materias primas limitadas o importadas. Esta característica lo convierte en una solución con alto potencial de escalabilidad a largo plazo y en una palanca estratégica para reforzar la autonomía energética europea. Además, puede utilizarse con las aeronaves y la infraestructura de repostaje existentes, facilitando su implantación en el sector.

En el caso de Eco2fly, el proyecto está diseñado para la creación de una cadena de valor integrada para la producción de eSAF en España. Un proceso que se inicia con la captura de CO₂ procedente del proceso de fabricación del cemento, combinándolo con hidrógeno renovable para la producción de eSAF y su logística asociada. El proyecto conecta capacidades industriales, energéticas y logísticas para unir la descarbonización industrial con la del transporte aéreo e impulsar una cadena de valor nacional y europea para combustibles sostenibles.

Gloria Carreras, directora de ESG de Volotea, ha destacado que «el eSAF será imprescindible para alcanzar la descarbonización de la aviación a largo plazo, pero su desarrollo requiere acelerar las inversiones y aumentar la capacidad de producción en Europa. Este acuerdo con Eco2Fly refleja el compromiso de Volotea con el impulso de proyectos estratégicos que contribuyan a garantizar la disponibilidad futura de eSAF y reforzar la autonomía energética europea».

Por su parte, Javier Esteban, director del proyecto ECO2FLY, ha señalado que «la firma de este memorando con una aerolínea como Volotea valida nuestro modelo de producción de eSAF y supone un impulso decisivo para escalar la oferta de combustibles sintéticos en el mercado español y europeo. Eco2fly reúne capacidades industriales, energéticas y logísticas complementarias, gracias a la participación de Holcim, Eco2fly Power y Exolum, para producir en Europa los combustibles que necesita nuestra aviación. Más allá del impacto en reducción de emisiones, este proyecto contribuirá a disminuir la dependencia del queroseno fósil importado y a reforzar la autonomía estratégica y la independencia energética de la Unión Europea, en línea con los objetivos de REPowerEU».

title: Biocarburanti, lo studio TEHA-Eni: “Per l'Europa leva di sicurezza energetica e competitività”
description:
I biocarburanti da materie prime rinnovabili possono rappresentare per l’Europa non soltanto uno strumento di decarbonizzazione dei trasporti, ma anche una leva di sicurezza energetica, diversificazione degli approvvigionamenti e tutela della competitività industriale.
Secondo lo studio, le crisi degli ultimi anni hanno evidenziato come la dipendenza da tecnologie, materie prime e capacità produttive possa produrre conseguenze sistemiche e mettere a rischio la sicurezza energetica europea.
In questa prospettiva, i biocarburanti vengono considerati non soltanto una leva per ridurre le emissioni nei trasporti, ma anche uno strumento di diversificazione, sicurezza energetica e politica industriale.
“Una soluzione già disponibile per i trasporti” La sfida indicata dallo studio è conciliare la transizione energetica con la competitività industriale e con la sostenibilità economica e sociale.
I biocarburanti vengono quindi presentati come una soluzione complementare agli altri vettori energetici, in grado di rafforzare contemporaneamente sicurezza energetica e competitività industriale europea.
text:
I biocarburanti da materie prime rinnovabili possono rappresentare per l’Europa non soltanto uno strumento di decarbonizzazione dei trasporti, ma anche una leva di sicurezza energetica, diversificazione degli approvvigionamenti e tutela della competitività industriale. È il messaggio al centro dello studio realizzato da TEHA Group insieme a Eni e presentato nell’ambito del Forum di Cernobbio organizzato da TEHA.

Uno scenario energetico profondamente cambiato

Il punto di partenza dell’analisi è il mutamento dello scenario energetico globale rispetto alla fase in cui è stato concepito il Green Deal. Secondo lo studio, le crisi degli ultimi anni hanno evidenziato come la dipendenza da tecnologie, materie prime e capacità produttive possa produrre conseguenze sistemiche e mettere a rischio la sicurezza energetica europea. In questo quadro, biocarburanti come HVO, Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil, e SAF, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, vengono indicati come soluzioni già disponibili per diversificare le fonti di approvvigionamento, ridurre le emissioni di gas serra lungo la filiera e, allo stesso tempo, preservare capacità produttive e competenze industriali in Europa.

“Evitare di sostituire una dipendenza con un’altra”

Per Valerio De Molli, managing partner e Ceo di TEHA Group, l’Europa deve evitare che il percorso di transizione energetica si traduca semplicemente nel passaggio da una dipendenza a un’altra. “Una transizione che sostituisce una dipendenza con un’altra non rafforza il continente, ne trasferisce soltanto la vulnerabilità”, ha sottolineato De Molli. In questa prospettiva, i biocarburanti vengono considerati non soltanto una leva per ridurre le emissioni nei trasporti, ma anche uno strumento di diversificazione, sicurezza energetica e politica industriale.

Secondo De Molli, occorre quindi superare un approccio prevalentemente regolatorio e adottare una visione più pragmatica e industriale, capace di tenere conto anche dei nuovi rischi geopolitici.

“Una soluzione già disponibile per i trasporti”

La sfida indicata dallo studio è conciliare la transizione energetica con la competitività industriale e con la sostenibilità economica e sociale. In questo contesto, Stefano Ballista, Ceo di Enilive, ha evidenziato il carattere immediatamente disponibile dei biocarburanti. Questi combustibili, secondo Ballista, possono contribuire a ridurre le emissioni del settore dei trasporti lungo l’intera filiera, sono ampiamente disponibili, possono essere distribuiti attraverso le infrastrutture esistenti e risultano utilizzabili in gran parte delle motorizzazioni diesel attualmente in circolazione.

I biocarburanti vengono quindi presentati come una soluzione complementare agli altri vettori energetici, in grado di rafforzare contemporaneamente sicurezza energetica e competitività industriale europea.

Innovazione e riconversione industriale

L’esperienza maturata da Eni viene richiamata anche come esempio del ruolo che innovazione tecnologica, competenze industriali e professionalità possono avere nei processi di trasformazione. Secondo Ballista, la combinazione di questi fattori può contribuire a generare valore, occupazione e sviluppo sostenibile, sostenendo allo stesso tempo la capacità competitiva dell’Europa.

Le proposte ai policy maker europei

Lo studio formula infine una serie di proposte rivolte ai decisori europei, con l’obiettivo di passare da un’impostazione prevalentemente restrittiva a un approccio giudicato più pragmatico. Uno dei punti centrali riguarda il metodo di misurazione delle emissioni. Secondo l’analisi, l’Europa dovrebbe superare una valutazione concentrata soltanto sulle emissioni allo scarico e prendere invece in considerazione le emissioni generate lungo l’intera filiera, così da riconoscere anche il contributo immediato dei biocarburanti alla riduzione dei gas serra.

Sostenere tecnologie già mature e scalabili

Un altro indirizzo proposto riguarda le tecnologie da sostenere nel percorso di transizione. Lo studio sottolinea come il cambiamento non possa essere affidato esclusivamente a soluzioni destinate a raggiungere la piena maturità nel lungo periodo. L’indicazione è quindi quella di valorizzare anche tecnologie già disponibili, scalabili e capaci di produrre risultati misurabili. Parallelamente, viene evidenziata la necessità di trasformare la base industriale europea, sostenendo la conversione degli impianti esistenti in bioraffinerie e preservando capacità produttive, competenze professionali e occupazione.

Tracciabilità e dati reali per misurare la sostenibilità

L’ultima proposta riguarda la verifica della sostenibilità dei biocarburanti. Il documento indica la necessità di basare le valutazioni su dati reali, facendo ricorso a misurazioni sul campo, sistemi di tracciabilità e tecnologie digitali. L’obiettivo è riconoscere le produzioni realmente addizionali e quelle caratterizzate dai livelli di sostenibilità più elevati, inserendo così i biocarburanti in una strategia europea che tenga insieme decarbonizzazione, sicurezza degli approvvigionamenti e difesa della base industriale.

text:
Rolls-Royce Projects Significant Fuel Savings with Upgraded Airbus A350 Engine

Rolls-Royce has announced that its latest enhancements to the Trent XWB-84 EP engine, which powers the Airbus A350, could enable airlines operating fleets of 20 aircraft to save up to $10 million annually in fuel costs. The engine manufacturer revealed these projections during a roundtable event ahead of the Farnborough Airshow, emphasizing the improved thrust-specific fuel consumption (SFC) achieved through recent upgrades.

Initially targeting a 1% improvement in SFC, Rolls-Royce now reports gains of up to 1.8%. Rob Watson, President of Civil Aerospace at Rolls-Royce, explained that a 1% improvement in SFC corresponds to nearly $500,000 in annual fuel savings per aircraft. For airlines with larger A350 fleets, these efficiencies could translate into substantial cost reductions amid ongoing volatility in jet fuel prices.

Engine Performance and Environmental Impact

The Trent XWB-84 EP entered service last year with Delta Air Lines as the launch customer and has since accumulated over 100,000 operational hours. Renowned for its industry-leading fuel efficiency and reliability, the engine has been selected by 90% of profitable airlines operating the A350. Notably, the Trent XWB-84 EP is capable of operating with up to 50% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), with a long-term goal of achieving 100% SAF compatibility. This capability positions the engine as a forward-looking option for carriers seeking to reduce carbon emissions and environmental impact.

Industry Challenges and Market Dynamics

Despite these advancements, some challenges persist for airlines considering the new engine. Emirates has expressed concerns regarding long-term engine durability, while United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby has highlighted ongoing engine shortages that could complicate fleet planning and operations. These issues illustrate the complexities airlines face when integrating new technology, even as they aim to benefit from fuel savings and environmental improvements.

Market response to the enhanced Trent XWB-84 EP has been largely positive, with growing interest in the Airbus A350-900 as carriers pursue fleet modernization and cost reduction strategies. However, competition remains intense. General Electric continues to dominate the Boeing 787 market, influencing airline and manufacturer decisions on engine selection and potentially shaping future developments within the widebody aircraft segment.

Investment and Certification

Rolls-Royce’s $1.33 billion (£1 billion) investment in the Trent XWB-84 EP program underscores its commitment to continuous innovation. The engine received certification from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) in December 2024, following extensive redevelopment and thousands of hours of rigorous ground and flight testing. These improvements not only enhance fuel efficiency and reduce emissions but also contribute to quieter and more reliable operations for airlines worldwide.

As the aviation industry confronts increasing pressure to enhance sustainability and manage operational costs, advancements in engine technology such as those embodied by the Trent XWB-84 EP will be pivotal in shaping the future of long-haul air travel.
